Why it matters: the ultimate's value is restoring HP that was lost, and the 8-second window lets you relink with enhanced Immersion while it lasts. Cast too early and the healing is wasted on full-HP allies; cast too late and someone has already died.
::curve 3,4,4 | His healing scales with skill level and items, so he gets stronger as fights get bigger.
## How the kit fits together
Estes works in a loop: link someone, gain defense and speed, charge the scripture faster, use the charged attack to slow a diver, and use the domain's edge to slow anyone who tries to reach the link target. The ultimate is a reset button that turns a losing exchange into a winning one by restoring several allies at once and letting him keep relinking while enhanced.
The question every fight asks is: who is the enemy trying to kill, and can I keep that person alive for long enough? Healing on its own does not win fights. Healing that outlasts the enemy's burst cooldowns does, because once their burst is spent, your team is fighting a team with no tools left.
## Combos and sequences
::combo Save a diving carry | S1 > S2 > BA | Link the carry, drop the domain between them and the diver so the edge slows the chaser, then use an empowered basic attack if it is charged.
Why it works: the link restores the carry immediately and keeps restoring them while the diver attacks. The domain placed between them makes the diver cross the edge and eat the 90% slow, which breaks the chase. If the scripture is charged, the enhanced attack adds a 60% slow on top, which gives the carry several seconds to walk away or turn the fight.
::combo Teamfight reset | ULT > S1 > S1 | Ultimate after the enemy burst lands, then keep relinking the lowest ally while Moonlight Immersion is enhanced.
Why it works: the ultimate applies an enhanced link to every ally near him, and Immersion stays enhanced for the 8-second window. Relinking the ally who is taking the most damage during that window gives a second, focused burst of healing. The enemy spent their burst before the ultimate; your team now has their HP back.
## Builds and emblems
::build Sustain support | Tough Boots, Fleeting Time, Flask of the Oasis, Oracle, Dominance Ice, Immortality | Flask of the Oasis adds an emergency shield when a healed ally is below 35% HP; Fleeting Time shortens his ultimate after kills or assists; Oracle increases healing he receives; Dominance Ice cuts enemy healing and shields around him.
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Agility, Pull Yourself Together, Focusing Mark | Agility helps him keep up with the link range; Pull Yourself Together shortens spell and item cooldowns; Focusing Mark lets allies deal more damage to an enemy he hits.
::spells Flicker, Purify | Flicker is the escape he does not have in his kit; Purify keeps him alive through a single stun.
How to choose: the build is about making his healing count and keeping him in range of it. Flask of the Oasis adds a shield on top of heals for allies in danger, so it pairs well with the link. Fleeting Time brings the ultimate back sooner in fights where your team gets assists. Dominance Ice is the answer when the enemy has their own healer or sustain fighters. Purify is the right spell when one point-and-click stun on Estes loses the fight; Flicker when the enemy dives with mobility.
## Roaming and early game
Early, Estes is a weak duelist. Stand with the laner who needs sustain to win the lane, and use the link to keep them healthy through trades. A gold laner kept at high HP can trade aggressively, and Estes's healing turns small trades into won trades.
Before objectives, use the domain on brush to reveal enemies inside it. A domain cast on a brush around the Turtle or Lord is cheap vision for a team about to walk in.
::map vision | Domain of Moon Goddess reveals enemies inside it: use it to check brushes around objectives before your team walks in.
## Teamfights
In teamfights, stand behind your frontline and within link range of your carry. Your two priorities, in order, are: keep the carry alive, and keep the frontline alive long enough for the carry to deal damage. Do not walk forward to deal damage yourself. The domain is for the space between the enemy divers and your backline, and the ultimate is for the moment the enemy's burst has landed on several of your heroes.
If the enemy has a hard engage tank, expect them to dive you rather than your carry. Stay beside your own tank or fighter so that a dive on you is also a dive into your team.
## Decision-making by game state
When you are ahead, your job is to keep your team fighting for objectives without losing anyone; a team that never dies keeps its lead. When you are behind, stand near turrets and make the enemy dive through the domain edge and your team's control. When the game is even, the team with an ultimate available usually wins the next fight, so track your ultimate cooldown and tell your team when it is up.
## Advanced techniques
- Link the frontline first: a link on the tank who is about to take damage gives you defense and speed and charges the scripture faster, which lets you peel with the enhanced attack sooner.
- Domain edges: place the domain so that the diver is already inside when it lands; they then must cross the edge to reach your carry or to escape.
- Ultimate timing: wait for the enemy to commit their burst before you ultimate. An ultimate cast before the fight is mostly wasted.
- Range discipline: the link breaks if you walk too far away. Do not chase a fleeing enemy with your carry; stay where the link holds.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Lunox,Pharsa,Valentina,Yve | bad=Baxia,Hayabusa,Franco,Saber | ally=Uranus,Masha,Yu Zhong,Thamuz
Why the good matchups are good: Lunox, Pharsa, Valentina and Yve deal their damage over time or in poke, and Estes can heal through damage that comes in pieces. Every heal undoes part of their pressure.
Why the bad matchups are bad: Baxia cuts healing, which undoes his main tool. Hayabusa and Saber dive and burst him or his carry before the heal matters, and Franco's hook pulls him out of his team where no one can protect him.
Why the allies work: Uranus, Masha, Yu Zhong and Thamuz are sustain fighters and tanks who stay in fights for a long time; Estes's healing makes them nearly impossible to kill.
Playing against Estes: buy healing reduction early, burst a single target instead of spreading damage, and dive Estes himself when he has no Flicker.
## Common mistakes
- Ultimate too early: healing full-HP allies wastes the ultimate.
- Walking forward: Estes has no escape; the frontline is not his place.
- Linking the wrong ally: the link belongs to whoever is about to be hit.
- Ignoring anti-heal: when the enemy buys it, his healing is reduced, so positioning and the domain's slow become more important than raw healing.

guides.title: Saber
guides.sub: Point-and-click assassin who deletes one target, then needs his team to survive
guides.body:
## Identity: what Saber is and why he is picked
Saber is a physical melee assassin who plays the jungle or roam. His identity is simple and his ultimate defines it: Triple Sweep charges at a target hero, knocks them airborne for 1.2 seconds, and hits them three times. It is targeted, so it cannot miss once cast, and the target cannot act during the knock-up. Combined with orbiting swords that fly at whatever he hits, it gives Saber one of the most reliable single-target bursts in the game.
He is picked to delete an immobile carry or mage. He is weak before his ultimate, weak into heroes who can survive his burst, and has a very obvious engage: once he has used his ultimate, he is a melee hero with a dash and nothing else.
## Kit deep-dive
### Enemy's Bane (passive)
Saber's attacks reduce enemies' physical defense on hit for 5 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. How to use it: hitting a target several times before the burst finishes increases the damage of everything after. Why it matters: his combo hits a target many times in quick succession (swords, ultimate strikes, Charge, enhanced attack), which builds stacks quickly, and the defense reduction is what makes the end of the combo lethal.
### Orbiting Swords (Skill 1)
Saber shoots out 5 swords that orbit around him, damaging enemies on contact. After roughly 5 seconds, they return. During the skill, whenever he deals damage with basic attacks or skills, he sends an orbiting sword at the target, dealing heavy damage to the main target and 50% to others it passes through, and reducing Charge's cooldown by 1 second. Swords deal only 50% damage to non-hero enemies.
How to use it: cast the swords before the burst, so that every hit during the ultimate sends another sword. Why it matters: the swords are much of his damage, and each one also reduces Charge's cooldown, which can give him a second Charge to chase or escape.
### Charge (Skill 2)
Saber dashes in a direction, damaging enemies on the path and enhancing his next basic attack, which deals damage and slows the target by 60% for 1 second. How to use it: Charge is both his gap-closer before the ultimate and his finisher or escape after it. Why it matters: the slow keeps a target that survived the combo in reach of a final basic attack.
### Triple Sweep (Ultimate)
Saber charges at a target enemy hero, knocking them airborne for 1.2 seconds and striking 3 times, with the third strike dealing the most damage. How to use it: it is targeted, so the only question is whether the target dies. Why it matters: the knock-up prevents the target from using skills or flash during it, so a target who would escape any other assassin cannot escape this one if the damage is there.
::curve 3,5,3 | Weak before level 4, very strong from his first ultimate into the mid game, and less decisive late when targets build defense.
## How the kit fits together
Saber's burst is a sequence of stacking hits: swords first so every later hit sends another sword, then the ultimate's three strikes, then Charge and the enhanced attack. Each hit adds a passive stack, reducing physical defense, so the last hits of the combo deal more damage than the first.
The decision is always the same: will this combo kill this target? If yes, commit. If no, wait until it will, or until someone else has softened the target. A Saber who uses his ultimate without killing is a Saber with no escape in the middle of the enemy team.
## Combos
::combo Standard burst | S1 > ULT > BA > S2 > BA | Swords first so they fly at the target during Triple Sweep, then basic attack, Charge and the empowered attack.
Why it works: the swords must be active before the ultimate so every strike sends a sword. The ultimate's knock-up holds the target while strikes and swords land and passive stacks build. Charge and the enhanced attack finish them, and the 60% slow keeps a survivor in reach.
::combo Flicker pick | S1 > Flicker > ULT > S2 | Cast swords, Flicker into range, ultimate, then use Charge to finish or escape.
Why it works: enemies stand just outside Saber's visible range. Flicker extends it unexpectedly, and the targeted ultimate lands before they react. Charge is saved for the end: chase if they survive, escape if help arrives.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst assassin | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Blade of the Heptaseas, Immortality | Blade of the Heptaseas' Ambush adds a big first-hit bonus after five seconds out of combat, which suits his engage; Blade of Despair rewards finishing low targets; Malefic Roar penetrates armor.
::emblem Custom Assassin Emblem | Rupture, Seasoned Hunter, Killing Spree | Penetration, faster objectives, and a heal and speed after damaging a low-HP target.
::spells Retribution, Flicker | Retribution when jungling; Flicker when roaming for surprise ultimates.
How to choose: Saber wants burst and penetration; his passive already reduces defense, and Malefic Roar adds more. Blade of the Heptaseas rewards waiting out of combat before engaging, which matches how Saber plays: hide, then strike once.
## Early game
Before level 4, Saber has no ultimate and is a weak duelist. Clear efficiently, help lanes only where the enemy is low, and avoid fights with stronger early junglers. Once he has his ultimate, his game begins.
Orbiting Swords deal only 50% damage to non-hero enemies, so his early clear is slower than his hero damage suggests. Use Charge to move between camps and to finish monsters, and do not waste time chasing early skirmishes you cannot win. The goal of the first minutes is to reach level 4 on time with Retribution ready, so that the first time the enemy carry walks up alone, your ultimate is waiting. A Saber who falls behind on levels arrives at his power spike late, after the enemy carry has bought the defense that makes his burst unreliable.
## Mid game: hunting
At level 4 and beyond, rotate through the river toward the lane where the enemy carry is overextended. Look for a carry or mage who is alone or at the edge of their team, and especially one without a dash or cleanse.
::map rotate | After reaching level 4, rotate through the river to the lane where the enemy carry is overextended.
Track the enemy's crowd control: Saber's combo uses his ultimate, so a hero who can lock him immediately after punishes him hard.
## Teamfights
In teamfights, Saber should not engage first. Wait for the enemy to use their control on your frontline, then ultimate their carry. If the carry is surrounded by tanks with control still up, look for a mage or support at the edge instead. Every kill Saber makes early in a fight turns it into a numbers advantage.
## Reading the fight: the kill check
Before every ultimate, run the same short check. First, the target: is it a hero whose HP and defense your full sequence can remove? Immobile marksmen and mages usually are; fighters and tanks usually are not until you are well ahead. Second, the protection: who on the enemy team can lock you the moment you land, and have they used that skill? A tank whose stun is on cooldown is not a threat for the next few seconds; one whose stun is ready will hold you in place while their team kills you. Third, the exit: if the target dies, can you get out? Charge's cooldown is shortened by every sword hit, so after a full combo you often have it back, but only if the swords were active during the ultimate.
If all three answers are good, commit without hesitation, because Saber's burst only works when it is fast. If any answer is bad, wait. Showing yourself on the edge of a fight without committing is still useful: the enemy carry who sees you has to stand closer to their tanks, which makes them less effective.
## Decision-making by game state
When ahead, his burst kills even tankier targets; invade and catch the enemy jungler. When behind, stay with your team and look for one pick only when the enemy carry is alone. When even, play around vision; Saber's best moments come from flanks the enemy does not see.
## Advanced techniques
- Sword timing: swords last roughly 5 seconds, so cast them just before engaging, not while walking.
- Charge resets: each sword hit reduces Charge's cooldown, so a full combo can bring Charge back for an escape.
- Target discipline: if the combo does not kill, do not commit. A Saber who ultimates a tank has thrown his most valuable skill.
- Stealth approach: brush and flanks hide his engage; the enemy should not see him before the ultimate.
- Passive stacking: Enemy's Bane stacks up to 5 times, so the strikes and swords early in the combo make the final enhanced attack hit hardest. Do not open with Charge if you can open with swords and the ultimate.
- Retribution steals: his burst plus Retribution can take a contested Turtle, but only commit when the enemy jungler has no way to lock you during it.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Pharsa,Odette | bad=Diggie,Khufra,Chou,Belerick | ally=Tigreal,Atlas,Franco,Pharsa
Why the good matchups are good: Miya, Layla, Pharsa and Odette are immobile backliners who cannot escape a targeted knock-up, and they have the least HP to survive the burst.
Why the bad matchups are bad: Diggie's ultimate frees his team from control; Khufra, Chou and Belerick have control that locks him right after his burst, which leaves him with no escape.
Why the allies work: Tigreal, Atlas and Franco start fights and draw enemy control, letting Saber enter freely; Pharsa adds long-range damage after his pick.
Playing against Saber: stay close to your frontline when he has his ultimate, buy defense once he is ahead, and save control for when he lands his burst.
## Common mistakes
- Ultimate on the wrong target: a tank survives; a carry dies.
- Swords too early: they return after roughly 5 seconds.
- Engaging first: Saber needs the enemy's control used first.
- Forcing fights before level 4: he is weak without his ultimate.

guides.title: Obsidia
guides.sub: Bone-shard marksman who banks damage, then cashes it all in on one basic attack
guides.body:
## Identity: what Obsidia is and why she is picked
Obsidia is a physical ranged marksman whose damage works like a savings account. Every hit she lands builds Bone Energy, every 30 Energy becomes a Bone Shard, she can hold up to 25 shards, and her next basic attack sends every stored shard at the target at once. Each shard deals physical damage and carries 7% of her attack effects. So the damage of any single basic attack depends on what she has banked before it, and a patient Obsidia hits far harder than her items alone suggest.
She is picked because her two basic skills have short cooldowns and her ultimate does something few marksmen can: it tethers her to an enemy hero, stops that hero from using displacement skills, and gives her extra shards and freedom of movement for 3s. That makes her a carry who can lock down a dash-reliant diver instead of simply running from them.
Her weakness is that her damage takes time to build and her escape is a very short burst of speed. Assassins who can burst her before she has banked shards, or who can reach her through the tether's limits, punish her hard.
## Kit deep-dive
### Return to Bone (passive)
When Obsidia deals damage she gains Bone Energy: basic attacks on non-hero units give 1, on heroes give 2, and skills give 3 times that. Hitting creeps gives none. At 30 Energy a Bone Shard forms, up to 25 shards. When she basic attacks, all shards strike the target, each dealing physical damage and inheriting 7% attack effects.
How to use it: build shards on minions and with skills while out of danger, then cash them in on a hero. Why it matters: the jungle creeps give nothing, so she builds on minions and heroes. And because a basic attack spends everything, attacking a minion by accident wastes the bank. Watch your auto-target in fights.
### Abyssal Bone Needle (Skill 1)
Obsidia launches a needle that deals 325 physical damage to enemies hit and triggers Return to Bone on the first enemy hero hit. How to use it: it is a skill shot that also cashes in your shards at range, which makes it her poke and her finisher. Why it matters: since skills give 3 times the Energy, landing it also builds the next round of shards. Its short cooldown means needle, attack, needle, attack is her main damage pattern.
### Phantom Shadowmeld (Skill 2)
Obsidia descends into the Abyss and gains 500% movement speed for 0.3s. How to use it: it is a short sidestep. Use it to dodge a skill shot or reposition one step, not to run across the map. Why it matters: the short cooldown means it is available often, and during her ultimate it is enhanced to last 1s with its cooldown cut to 33%.
### Hunt of Bone (Ultimate)
Obsidia shoots Bones of Wrath in a direction, dealing 125 physical damage, briefly stunning the first enemy hero hit, and pulling herself near them. The bones then tether her to the enemy: she cannot move more than 4 units away, the enemy cannot use displacement skills, and their movement drags her along. During the tether she gains 5 temporary shards, can move through obstacles and attack while moving, and Shadowmeld is enhanced. It lasts 3s.
How to use it: it is a commitment. You are pulled in close, so use it on a target you can kill or must stop. Why it matters: the target cannot dash away, and the temporary shards plus enhanced Shadowmeld turn those 3s into her highest damage window.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, solid once she has her core items, and strongest late when every shard strike carries full attack effects.
## How the kit fits together
Obsidia's loop is build, then spend. Needle and basic attacks on minions build shards; a basic attack or needle on a hero spends them. The ultimate is a guaranteed spending window: the target cannot dash, she gets free shards, and she can keep attacking while moving. Shadowmeld is the safety valve that keeps her alive between spends.
The key judgement is when to spend. Spending on a target at full HP behind their tank deals damage but does not change the fight. Spending a full bank on a target already in trouble usually kills them.
## Combos
::combo Poke and cash in | S1 > BA > S1 > BA | Needle builds Energy and triggers stored shards; each basic attack after it sends the rest.
Why it works: the needle triggers Return to Bone at range, so stored shards hit before the enemy can close in. Each skill hit builds Energy faster than basic attacks, so needle, attack, needle, attack keeps shards forming and spending in a cycle.
::combo Lock-down kill | ULT > BA > S2 > BA > S1 > BA | Tether the target, attack while Shadowmeld keeps you moving, finish with Needle.
Why it works: the tether stops the target's escape skills and gives 5 temporary shards. Enhanced Shadowmeld lasts longer during the tether and its cooldown is shorter, so you can keep moving while attacking and dodge the target's answers, then finish with the needle.
::combo Reposition | S2 > BA > S1 | Step out of a skillshot, then answer with an attack and Needle.
Why it works: Shadowmeld's short burst dodges a single skill, and the attack and needle right after punish the enemy while their skill is on cooldown.
## Builds and emblems
::build Attack-effect marksman | Swift Boots, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword, Golden Staff, Malefic Gun, Wind of Nature | Each shard inherits a share of attack effects, so on-hit items such as Corrosion Scythe and Demon Hunter Sword add to every withdrawal; Wind of Nature answers burst physical threats.
::build Crit option (test it) | Swift Boots, Berserker's Fury, Haas' Claws, Windtalker, Malefic Roar, Wind of Nature | Builds around her basic attacks instead of attack effects. Compare both in practice before committing.
::emblem Custom Marksman Emblem | Fatal, Weapon Master, Weakness Finder | Crit and attack, more value from items, and a slow on basic attacks to keep targets in range.
::spells Flicker, Inspire | Flicker for safety; Inspire for longer extended fights.
How to choose: since every shard inherits 7% of attack effects, items with on-hit effects add a little to every shard, which adds up when 25 strike at once. The crit option is labelled "test it" in the data because it has not been confirmed as better; try both in practice. Wind of Nature is for games where a physical assassin is the main threat.
## Laning
Obsidia plays the gold lane. Her lane plan is to build shards on the wave and spend them on the enemy marksman when they step up. Poke with the needle, which cashes in shards at range, then step back with Shadowmeld if they answer.
::map lane | Hold the gold lane; poke with Needle and step back with Shadowmeld.
Because creeps give no Energy, rotating to jungle camps does not build shards. Her bank comes from the wave and from heroes, so staying in lane early is important.
## Mid game
The mid game is when her items start to make each shard count, because each one carries part of her attack effects. In the mid game, Obsidia should stand behind her frontline and spend shards on whoever comes into range. Her ultimate is best used defensively against a diver: tether the assassin who jumps on you, and they can neither dash out nor dash further, while you gain shards and keep attacking.
## Teamfights
In teamfights, enter with a full bank. Spend it on the nearest threat, usually the enemy frontline or a diver, and use the needle to cash in at range on the backline when possible. Save the ultimate for a dash-reliant hero who jumps on you or your team; it is your strongest single-target tool and your best answer to dives.
## Decision-making by game state
When ahead, push lanes and turrets with your bank; enemies who walk into range lose a big chunk of HP. When behind, stay with your frontline and use the ultimate on divers. When even, farm minions to keep your bank full and look for fights near objectives.
## Advanced techniques
- Bank management: avoid wasting shards on minions when a hero fight is about to start. Let the bank fill before you engage.
- Needle cash-in: the needle triggers your shards at range, so you can spend a full bank without stepping into danger. It triggers on the first enemy hero hit, so a minion in the way does not waste it.
- Tether as defense: the tether blocks displacement skills, so tethering a diver stops their escape and further dashes.
- Enhanced Shadowmeld: during the tether, Shadowmeld lasts 1s and comes back quickly; use it to dodge while you attack.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Ling,Lancelot,Fanny,Hayabusa | bad=Helcurt,Benedetta,Yin,Aldous,Hanzo | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Estes,Angela
The bad list is the official counter data for her in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment from her kit: dash-reliant heroes lose their escape during the tether.
Why the bad matchups are bad (assessment): Helcurt and Hanzo can burst her before she builds shards; Benedetta and Yin can reach her and lock or isolate her; Aldous can one-shot her late.
Why the allies work: Atlas and Tigreal group enemies for her to spend shards on; Estes and Angela keep her alive while she builds.
Playing against Obsidia: burst her before she stores shards, and fight her away from her frontline. Heroes who can lock or silence her before she attacks remove her damage.
## Common mistakes
- Spending shards on minions in a fight: watch your auto-target.
- Ultimate as an engage on a tank: it pulls you close; use it on a threat or a kill.
- Using Shadowmeld to run: it is a short sidestep.
- Farming jungle creeps for shards: creeps give no Energy.

guides.title: Eudora
guides.sub: Lightning mage whose Superconductor mark turns every skill into a two-part combo
guides.body:
## Identity: what Eudora is and why she is picked
Eudora is a magic ranged mage built for burst. Her passive, Superconductor, marks non-minion units hit by her skills for 5 seconds, and every skill does something extra against a marked target. That means her skills are not separate buttons but parts of one combo: the first skill marks, and every skill after it is stronger. Her kit is short-range compared with other mages, but in that range she deletes squishy targets, and her stun can spread to everyone near the target.
She is picked for picks: a short-range burst combo with a stun that can kill an immobile carry before they react. She is weak against tanks and magic defense, against enemies who stay out of her range, and against heroes who can reach her first.
## Kit deep-dive
### Superconductor (passive)
Eudora's skills inflict Superconductor on non-minion units for 5 seconds, and her skills trigger additional effects against marked targets. How to use it: always start with a skill that marks. Why it matters: every bonus in her kit (the lightning chain, the spreading stun, the Thunderburst) needs the mark, so opening with the wrong skill loses most of her damage.
### Forked Lightning (Skill 1)
A fan of lightning that deals magic damage (200% against minions). Against a marked target, Eudora forms a lightning chain, gaining 40% movement speed for up to 1 second; the chain deals damage over time and more when it ends, and if that end hit lands, the skill's cooldown is reduced by 50%. How to use it: the fan marks several targets, which sets up the spreading stun. On marked targets, the chain gives speed and extra damage and halves the cooldown, so Forked Lightning can be cast again quickly. Why it matters: it is both her opener and her refresh.
### Ball Lightning (Skill 2)
Eudora hurls an orb at a target enemy, reducing their magic defense for 1.8 seconds, dealing damage and stunning them for 1 second. Against a marked target, the orb reduces magic defense of nearby enemies, deals area damage around the target and stuns all nearby enemies. How to use it: always cast it on a marked target. Why it matters: on a marked target it becomes an area stun, which can catch several enemies standing together.
### Thunder's Wrath (Ultimate)
A blast of lightning on an area: heavy damage at the center, less outside it. Each time it hits a marked target, it triggers a Thunderburst on that target after a short delay. How to use it: cast it after the stun, on the center of the stunned group. Why it matters: on marked targets, the ultimate deals a second burst of damage, which is what finishes them.
::curve 4,5,3 | Strong early once she has her ultimate, very strong in mid-game pickoffs, and weaker late when enemies have magic defense and frontliners protect the carries.
## How the kit fits together
Eudora's combo is mark, stun, burst: Forked Lightning marks and chains, Ball Lightning stuns (and spreads the stun on a marked target), Thunder's Wrath bursts with Thunderbursts on marked targets. Every bonus depends on the mark, and the stun's magic defense reduction makes everything after it hit harder.
Her range is short, so the real skill is getting into range. Brush, flanks and Flicker are her tools for that.
## Combos
::combo Single-target burst | S1 > S2 > ULT | Mark with Forked Lightning, stun with Ball Lightning, finish with Thunder's Wrath.
Why it works: Forked Lightning marks the target, so Ball Lightning's stun reduces magic defense and holds them in place for the ultimate. The ultimate's Thunderburst on the marked target adds the final damage.
::combo Group stun | S1 > S2 > ULT > S1 | Hit several heroes with the fan so Ball Lightning stuns all of them, then ultimate and recast Forked Lightning if its cooldown was halved.
Why it works: the fan marks several heroes, so Ball Lightning on one of them stuns everyone nearby. The ultimate hits all of them and triggers a Thunderburst on each marked target, and Forked Lightning's halved cooldown lets you cast it again to finish.
::combo Flicker pick | Flicker > S2 > S1 > ULT | Flicker into range for the stun when the target is just out of reach.
Why it works: enemies stand just outside her short range. Flicker plus an immediate stun gives them no time to react; Forked Lightning then marks them and the ultimate finishes. The stun here is unmarked, so it hits only the target, which is acceptable for a single pick.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Lightning Truncheon, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Blood Wings | Lightning Truncheon's echo adds area damage; Genius Wand and Divine Glaive cut magic defense; Holy Crystal and Blood Wings add raw power and a shield.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and extra burst after hitting a target with several skills.
::spells Flicker | Flicker is the standard for a short-range stun mage.
How to choose: Eudora wants burst and magic penetration; her stun already reduces magic defense, and Genius Wand and Divine Glaive cut more. Blood Wings' shield is the closest thing she has to defense.
## Laning and rotations
Eudora plays mid. Clear the wave quickly (Forked Lightning deals 200% damage to minions), then rotate to the side lane that is being pushed.
::map rotate | Clear mid, then rotate to whichever side lane is being pushed.
Her rotations are her main value early: a mage who can stun and burst helps any lane get kills.
## The range problem and how to solve it
Eudora's combo only works from close range, and every enemy who has played against her knows it. That makes her approach the hardest part of playing her. There are three ways in. The first is brush: standing in a brush beside a path the enemy must take, then casting Forked Lightning as they pass, marks them before they know you are there. The second is your frontline: when your tank engages, the enemy turns toward the tank and stops watching the mage behind it, which gives you a step or two of free approach. The third is Flicker, which closes the last gap faster than anyone can react.
The wrong way in is walking straight at a target who can see you. They step back, your skills fall short, and you have spent your cooldowns for nothing while standing in front of their team.
## The magic defense window
Ball Lightning reduces the target's magic defense for 1.8 seconds. That window is short, and everything you cast inside it deals more damage. This is why the order matters: mark first, then stun, then ultimate immediately while the reduction is still on. Casting the ultimate a moment late, after the reduction has ended, can be the difference between a kill and a target escaping with a sliver of HP. Against a marked group, the reduction applies to everyone near the stunned target, so the ultimate right after a group stun hits a whole cluster with reduced magic defense.
## Mid game: picks
In the mid game, she hunts. Move through brush toward the enemy carry or mage, mark them with Forked Lightning, and stun them before they can react. When enemies are grouped, look for the group stun on a marked cluster.
## Reading the target
Not every target is worth the combo. Eudora's burst is decisive against marksmen, mages and supports with low HP and no escape, and it is wasted on a tank. Before committing, ask whether the target can survive the full sequence or escape the stun. A hero with a cleanse or an untargetable skill may avoid the stun, and if the stun misses, the ultimate is easy to dodge. In that case, wait until they use their escape on someone else. Fighters who build defense in the late game can also survive her burst, so late in the game the combo is best saved for the backline.
## Teamfights
In teamfights, Eudora must wait for an opening. Her range is short, so walking forward early gets her killed. Wait for the enemy to use their engage, then flank toward their backline and use the group stun on any cluster you can reach.
## Decision-making by game state
When ahead, her burst kills almost any squishy target; push your advantage with picks. When behind, stay near your team and burst divers who come to you. When even, focus on rotations and catching targets alone.
## Advanced techniques
- Always mark first: Ball Lightning and Thunder's Wrath gain their bonuses only on marked targets.
- Chain refresh: if the lightning chain's end hit lands, Forked Lightning's cooldown is halved, so you can recast it in the same fight.
- Group stun setup: hit several heroes with the fan, then stun the one in the middle.
- Brush approaches: her short range makes brush and flanks essential.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Cecilion,Odette | bad=Zilong,Floryn,Marcel,Helcurt,Aldous | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Franco,Chou
The bad list is the official counter data for her in Mythical Glory+; the good list is an assessment from her kit (immobile carries).
Why the bad matchups are bad (assessment): Zilong and Helcurt can reach her first; Floryn heals through her burst; Marcel's freeze undoes her combo; Aldous can survive and one-shot her later.
Why the allies work: Atlas, Tigreal, Franco and Chou group or lock enemies for her to stun and burst.
Playing against Eudora: keep distance, stand apart so her stun cannot spread, and buy magic defense if she is ahead.
## Common mistakes
- Opening with Ball Lightning: without the mark, it stuns only one target.
- Walking into fights early: her range is short.
- Ultimate before the stun: targets move out of the center.
- Ignoring the chain refresh: recasting Forked Lightning adds a lot of damage.

guides.title: Gloo
guides.sub: Slime tank that sticks to an enemy and makes them take the damage meant for him
guides.body:
## Identity: what Gloo is and why he is picked
Gloo is a magic melee tank who roams. His passive stacks Sticky on enemies hit by his skills, slowing them by 4% per stack for 6 seconds, up to 5 stacks, and each stack reduces their damage to Gloo by 4%. His ultimate unlocks only when an enemy hero has full Sticky stacks; then Gloo attaches to them for up to 9 seconds, recovering HP and transferring 80% of the damage he receives to them. A Gloo attached to an enemy carry makes the enemy team choose between hitting him (and their carry) or ignoring him.
He is picked for his control (immobilizes and drags) and his unusual ultimate. He is weak against burst that kills him before he builds stacks, and against teams who can peel him off.
## Kit deep-dive
### Stick, Stick (passive)
Each skill hit gives Sticky, slowing by 4% per stack for 6 seconds, up to 5. Each stack reduces the enemy's damage to Gloo by 4%. How to use it: hit the same target repeatedly to build stacks. Why it matters: full stacks unlock the ultimate and reduce the target's damage to him.
### Slam, Slam (Skill 1)
Gloo slams the ground, dealing 80 magic damage, then leaves a Goo that explodes after 3 seconds, dealing damage and immobilizing for 1 second. Touching the Goo explodes it immediately, resets the skill's cooldown, and heals him if it hits an enemy (more if it hits an enemy hero). How to use it: touch your Goo to reset Slam. Why it matters: the reset makes Slam a repeatable source of stacks and immobilizes.
### Spread, Spread (Skill 2)
Gloo splits into Goos, dealing damage in a fan and immobilizing for 0.5 seconds. While split, he gains 10% movement speed and deals 80 magic damage every 0.25 seconds to enemies he touches, for 4 seconds. If the skill hits a Goo, Gloo charges over to merge with it, dragging enemies in his path. How to use it: aim at your own Goo to drag enemies. Why it matters: the drag repositions enemies into your team.
### Grab, Grab (Ultimate)
Unlocked when any enemy hero has full Sticky stacks. Gloo attaches to the target for up to 9 seconds, recovering HP. His basic attacks deal magic damage, and he transfers 80% of the damage he receives (excluding turrets) to the host. If the target dies while attached, the cooldown is reduced to 5 seconds. How to use it: attach to the enemy carry or the hero your team is focusing. Why it matters: enemies who hit him hurt their own teammate.
::curve 4,4,4 | Steady across the game: strong control early, strong in fights mid, and a durable frontliner late.
## How the kit fits together
Gloo builds stacks with Slam and Spread, resets Slam by touching his Goo, drags enemies by aiming Spread at the Goo, and then attaches with the ultimate. The attached target takes most of the damage Gloo receives, so enemies must choose between hitting Gloo and protecting their teammate. A kill while attached brings the ultimate back in 5 seconds.
## Combos
::combo Stack and stick | S1 > S2 > S1 > ULT | Slam, spread into the Goo to drag, slam again for the reset and stacks, then attach.
Why it works: Slam leaves a Goo, Spread aimed at it drags the enemy toward it, and touching the Goo resets Slam for more stacks. With full stacks, the ultimate unlocks and Gloo attaches.
::combo Goo reset | S1 > S1 | Touch the Goo to explode it at once and reset Slam, Slam.
Why it works: touching the Goo explodes it immediately, resets the cooldown and heals him if it hits, which gives him two Slams in quick succession.
## Builds and emblems
::build Control tank | Tough Boots, Cursed Helmet, Dominance Ice, Radiant Armor, Antique Cuirass, Immortality | Cursed Helmet adds area damage while you stick to fights; Dominance Ice for grouped enemies; Radiant Armor and Antique Cuirass for defense; Immortality to stay in fights.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP and defense, plus extra damage on attacks.
::spells Flicker | Flicker is the standard engage tool.
How to choose: Gloo needs defense to build stacks and attach. Cursed Helmet suits him because he stays close to enemies.
## Roaming and early game
Early, Gloo roams with the jungler, setting up kills with immobilizes.
::map roam | Roam with your jungler early, setting up kills with immobilizes.
His Slam reset and Spread drag make him strong in skirmishes.
## How the stacks work in a real fight
The ultimate needs full Sticky stacks on one enemy hero, so the question in every fight is: can I land 5 skill hits on the same target? Each skill hit adds a stack, and the stacks last 6 seconds, so the hits must come close together. Slam, Slam hits once on cast and once when the Goo explodes. Spread, Spread hits in its fan and keeps hitting enemies Gloo touches every 0.25 seconds while split. Touching the Goo resets Slam, which gives another round of hits. A good sequence lands several stacks quickly: Slam, then Spread into the Goo, which drags the target and explodes it, resetting Slam, then Slam again.
Each stack also slows the target by 4% and reduces their damage to Gloo by 4%. At full stacks, that target is noticeably slowed and deals less damage to Gloo. So even before the ultimate, stacking the enemy's main damage dealer makes Gloo harder for them to kill.
## How the ultimate actually plays out
Once attached, Gloo stays on the target for up to 9 seconds, recovers HP, and transfers 80% of the damage he receives (except from turrets) to the host. This creates a dilemma for the enemy team. If they hit Gloo, most of that damage goes to their own teammate. If they ignore Gloo, he keeps attacking with converted basic attacks and his team focuses the host. Either way, the host is in trouble.
The right target for the attachment is the enemy hero your team is about to focus: the carry, the mage, or a diver who has jumped in. If your team kills the host while you are attached, the ultimate's cooldown drops to 5 seconds, so you can attach to the next target. That means a well-timed attachment in a teamfight can chain through several enemies.
The wrong target is a tank or a hero your team cannot reach. Attaching to a tank on the far side of the fight just takes Gloo out of it for several seconds.
## Being peeled and how to answer
The enemy's main answer to the attachment is to kill or remove Gloo before it happens, or to protect the host so that the damage Gloo transfers does not matter. Heroes with a cleanse can sometimes free themselves, and heroes with heavy burst can kill Gloo before he builds stacks. When you face those, play more patiently: build stacks on the target from behind your frontline, and attach only when the host's protectors have used their skills. If you attach to a host whose team has healing, the transferred damage may be healed back, so prioritize hosts away from the enemy healer.
Another detail is that turret damage is not transferred. Attaching to a host under their own turret means you take the turret's hits yourself, so avoid attaching there unless the kill is certain.
## Teamfights
In teamfights, Gloo builds stacks on the enemy carry or the hero your team wants to focus. Once stacks are full, attach. Enemies who hit you hurt their own teammate, and you heal while attached.
## Decision-making by game state
When ahead, attach to enemy carries to end fights quickly. When behind, protect your carry with immobilizes and drags. When even, play around objectives and look for stack opportunities.
## Advanced techniques
- Goo positioning: place Goos where you want to drag enemies with Spread.
- Slam resets: touch your Goo to get more stacks quickly.
- Attach target: choose the enemy your team is focusing; the damage transfer helps them finish.
- Cooldown reset: a kill while attached brings the ultimate back in 5 seconds.
- Split movement: while Spread, Spread is active, Gloo moves 10% faster and damages enemies he touches every 0.25 seconds, so walking through the enemy backline while split builds stacks on several targets at once.
- Healing from Goo: touching a Goo that hits an enemy hero heals him more than hitting a minion, so in a long fight keep resetting Slam on heroes to stay healthy until the attachment. This is also why Gloo is hard to trade with in lane: every reset is a little more HP for him.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Aulus,Zhuxin,Lancelot,Ling | bad=Aamon,Jawhead,Johnson,Karina,Chang'e | ally=Eudora,Pharsa,Claude,Moskov
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+; Gloo also appears in the official counter lists for Aulus and Zhuxin, which is the basis of the good list.
Why the good matchups are good: Aulus, Zhuxin, Lancelot and Ling must stay close to deal damage, which lets Gloo build stacks on them quickly, and the stacks reduce their damage to him.
Why the bad matchups are bad (assessment): Aamon and Karina can burst him or his host, Jawhead and Johnson can grab or move him out of position, and Chang'e deals damage from range where Gloo struggles to build stacks.
Why the allies work: Eudora, Pharsa, Claude and Moskov deal heavy damage to targets Gloo has stuck to or immobilized.
Playing against Gloo: avoid standing in his Goo, kill him before he builds full stacks, and do not hit him while he is attached to your carry unless the damage is worth it.
## Common mistakes
- Attaching too early: it needs full stacks.
- Forgetting the Goo reset: touch the Goo for another Slam.
- Attaching to a tank: attach to a carry or the focus target.
- Not using the drag: aim Spread at your Goo.

guides.title: Sun
guides.sub: Clone fighter who shreds armor, splits pushes and wins long side-lane duels
guides.body:
## Identity: what Sun is and why he is picked
Sun is a melee physical fighter for the EXP lane or jungle who fights with Doppelgangers. His passive, **Simian God**, reduces the physical defense of enemies hit by Sun and his clones by 5% per stack, up to 6 stacks, and heals Sun each time a Doppelganger deals damage. Basic attacks from Sun and his clones also deal extra damage to creeps, which helps his jungle clear.
**Endless Variety** throws his Golden Staff, which becomes a Doppelganger that lasts 5 seconds where it lands or hits. **Swift Exchange** throws the staff the other way: a Doppelganger appears where Sun stood, and Sun conceals himself and travels with the staff. The two skills share one cooldown. **Instantaneous Move** commands every Doppelganger to strike the target with him, counting as basic-attack damage, so it triggers attack effects. His ultimate, **Clone Techniques**, summons a stronger Doppelganger that lasts 8 seconds and inherits 70%-100% of his attributes, though it takes increased damage.
Why he is picked: armor shred plus many attack-effect hits make him a strong duelist and a fast pusher, especially into teams that stack physical defense. His weakness: his clones die to area damage, and crowd control on Sun ends the fight before the clones matter.
## Kit deep-dive
### Simian God (passive)
The defense shred stacks from every clone hit, so a fight with three clones shreds faster than a fight with one. The healing comes from clone damage, so clones are also his sustain.
### Endless Variety and Swift Exchange (Skills 1 and 2)
One cooldown, two directions. Use Endless Variety to engage (the clone appears on the target) and Swift Exchange to disengage or to bait (the clone stays, Sun hides).
### Instantaneous Move (Skill 3)
Short cooldown, and the core of his damage: every clone strikes with him and the hits count as basic attacks.
### Clone Techniques (Ultimate)
The strongest clone. Summon it at the start of a duel so it fights the whole time.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, strong mid game once he has attack-effect items, and very strong late as a split pusher.
## Combos
::combo Duel opener | ULT > S1 > S3 > BA > S3 | Big clone first, staff clone onto the target, then strike with every clone.
::combo Bait and switch | S2 > S3 > BA | Leave a clone, move concealed with the staff, then strike from a new angle.
## Builds and emblems
::build Attack-effect duelist | Warrior Boots, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword, Golden Staff, Sea Halberd, Malefic Roar | Clones inherit a portion of attack effects and Instantaneous Move triggers them, so on-hit items scale every strike; Sea Halberd cuts enemy healing.
::build Durable split push | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword, Antique Cuirass, Immortality | More HP and defense for side lanes where he fights alone.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing on skill damage for long duels.
::spells Retribution, Petrify | Retribution when jungling; Petrify in the EXP lane to lock a target while the clones strike.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
In the EXP lane, trade when your skills are up and the enemy is in range of all your clones. In the jungle, the extra creep damage on basic attacks speeds up clears.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane and push the wave with clones.
## Mid game and teamfights
Sun is better at split pushing than at front-to-back teamfights. Push a side lane while your team holds mid, and join fights only when the enemy's area damage has been spent. In fights, focus the target your team is already hitting so the armor shred adds up.
## Advanced techniques
- Clone counting: the number of active clones decides your damage. Wait for your ultimate before committing.
- Concealed travel: Swift Exchange conceals you, which lets you dodge targeted skills or reposition behind a target.
- Turret pressure: clones help push a lane very quickly when you are alone.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Belerick,Tigreal,Franco,Hylos | bad=Jawhead,Harley,Hanzo,Diggie,Layla | ally=Estes,Angela,Diggie,Mathilda
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: tanks who rely on physical defense lose much of it to the shred.
Playing against Sun: use area damage to clear the clones, control Sun himself, and do not duel him when he has his ultimate up.
## Situational adjustments
- Against healers: Sea Halberd early.
- Against heavy control: build defense and lean on split pushing instead of teamfights.
- When ahead: push towers while the enemy is busy elsewhere.
## Practice drills
- Clone drill: practice summoning all clones and striking with Instantaneous Move.
- Swift Exchange drill: practice repositioning concealed behind a dummy.
## Common mistakes
- Fighting without the ultimate.
- Clumping clones in enemy area damage.
- Joining every fight instead of pushing.

guides.title: Lukas
guides.sub: Beast-form fighter who stays in fights by healing on each skill hit
guides.body:
## Identity: what Lukas is and why he is picked
Lukas is a melee physical fighter for the EXP lane or jungle. His passive, **Hero's Resolve**, gives him Resolve every second and extra Resolve when he damages heroes, and his Sacred Beast form consumes Resolve each second it stays active.
**Flash Combo** is enhanced by up to two basic attacks (stored as Vigor for 4 seconds). Casting it consumes the stacks for a hit that heals 8% of his max HP when it hits a hero; with one stack it pulls the target, with two it adds more strikes. **Flash Step** dashes and turns his next basic attack into a gap-closing strike that grants 20% movement speed and 20% attack speed for 4 seconds, with lightning on his basic attacks. His ultimate, **Unleash the Beast**, turns him into the Sacred Beast: more base movement speed, all attributes increased by 15%, and new skill effects. While transformed, he can recast to fire a Shockwave Blast for 450 physical damage.
Why he is picked: he sustains through fights with healing on each hero hit, and his beast form makes him faster and tougher at the moment fights start. His weakness: he is melee with limited control, so kiting and burst before he reaches you beat him.
## Kit deep-dive
### Hero's Resolve (passive)
Fighting heroes fuels his transformation. Long fights keep him in Beast form longer.
### Flash Combo (Skill 1)
Weave basic attacks before casting to store stacks. Each hero hit heals him, which is his main sustain.
### Flash Step (Skill 2)
Your gap closer. The attack-speed and movement-speed buff afterwards is what lets him stick to targets.
### Unleash the Beast (Ultimate)
Transform before or as the fight starts, then use the Shockwave Blast to finish runners.
::curve 4,4,4 | Strong lane presence early, solid in mid-game skirmishes and still a durable frontline fighter late.
## Combos
::combo Stacked combo | S2 > BA > BA > S1 | Dash in, store two stacks with attacks, then cast the enhanced combo.
::combo Beast opener | ULT > S2 > BA > BA > S1 > ULT | Transform, close the gap, stack and combo, then Shockwave Blast to finish.
## Builds and emblems
::build Sustain fighter | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Hunter Strike, Brute Force Breastplate, Queen's Wings, Immortality | War Axe and Brute Force Breastplate reward long fights; Queen's Wings and Immortality keep him alive while he heals.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing on skill damage.
::spells Petrify, Retribution | Petrify in lane; Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Trade with stacked Flash Combos so each exchange heals you. Avoid trading when Flash Step is on cooldown, as you need it to reach ranged opponents.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane and use your sustain to win trades.
## Mid game and teamfights
Transform when the fight begins, dive onto the backline or peel for your carry, and keep hitting heroes to keep healing. Do not transform too early: Resolve drains each second.
## Advanced techniques
- Stack before combo: basic attacks before Flash Combo make it stronger and give the pull.
- Resolve management: transforming at the right moment matters more than transforming quickly.
- Shockwave finish: the 450-damage blast catches enemies who flee.
- Pull with one stack: a one-stack Flash Combo pulls the target toward you, which is useful when a ranged hero is about to step out of range. Two stacks give more damage but no pull, so choose by the situation.
- Beast form duration: because Resolve drains each second in beast form and is refilled by damaging heroes, staying in contact with enemies is what keeps the transformation going.
## Draft and team fit
Lukas is a solo-queue threat more than a pro pick: banned in 52.22% of ranked Mythical Glory+ games over the past 7 days, but picked only 3 times (1 win) in the MPL PH S18 playoffs. He fits drafts that need a durable fighter who can also chase, and he pairs well with a roamer who can lock targets for his combo. Against teams with heavy anti-heal or long-range poke, a fighter with more control may serve your team better.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Sun | bad=Ling,Natalia,Zilong,Fanny,Harith | ally=Estes,Angela,Atlas,Tigreal
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: melee fighters who cannot escape his sustain in long trades.
Playing against Lukas: kite him, burst him before he heals, and use anti-heal.
## Situational adjustments
- Against anti-heal: build more defense rather than relying on healing.
- Against ranged teams: use Flash Step carefully and wait for your team's engage.
- When ahead: invade the jungle with your jungler.
## Practice drills
- Stack drill: practice two basic attacks then Flash Combo.
- Transform timing drill: practice transforming at the start of fights, not before.
## Common mistakes
- Using Flash Combo without stacks.
- Transforming too early.
- Chasing too far without vision.

guides.title: Aulus
guides.sub: Axe fighter who gets stronger with every skill hit and refuses to be stopped
guides.body:
## Identity: what Aulus is and why he is picked
Aulus is a melee physical fighter for the jungle or EXP lane. His passive, **Fighting Spirit**, gives 2 seconds of enhanced basic attacks after each skill damages a unit (accumulating up to 4 seconds). Enhanced attacks gain range and attack speed, slam a line, slow, and heal 30 HP per hit.
**Aulus, Charge!** removes slows and grants 30% movement speed for 5 seconds; if he takes no hard control in the first 2 seconds, he becomes Enraged and immune to control for the rest. **The Power of Axe** swings in a fan, stuns for 0.3 seconds and slows by 30% for 2 seconds; recast to dash and smash. His ultimate, **Cleaving Axe**, swings repeatedly at nearby enemies, then unleashes a wider slash; during it he gains 20-40% damage reduction and short bursts of movement speed.
Why he is picked: he is hard to stop once Enraged, and his ultimate is a strong area teamfight tool. His weakness: hard control in the first 2 seconds of Charge stops the immunity.
## Kit deep-dive
### Fighting Spirit (passive)
Every skill hit extends enhanced attacks. Weave skills to keep the enhanced attacks active.
### Aulus, Charge! (Skill 1)
Your engage. Avoid control in the first 2 seconds to become Enraged.
### The Power of Axe (Skill 2)
Your control and gap closer.
### Cleaving Axe (Ultimate)
Your teamfight tool. Use it in the middle of enemies.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, strong mid game and very strong late as a durable fighter.
## Combos
::combo Charge engage | S1 > S2 > S2 > ULT | Charge in, swing and smash, then ultimate.
::combo Enhanced attacks | S2 > BA > BA > S2 > BA | Skill hits extend enhanced attacks.
## Builds and emblems
::build Durable fighter | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Hunter Strike, Brute Force Breastplate, Queen's Wings, Immortality | Sustain and damage for long fights.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing on skill damage.
::spells Retribution, Petrify | Retribution in the jungle; Petrify in lane.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Farm efficiently and look for ganks once you have your ultimate. Each skill that hits a camp also extends your enhanced attacks, and those attacks heal 30 HP per hit, so weaving skills between attacks keeps you healthy through the clear. Gank lanes where the enemy has used their control skill: Charge only becomes control immunity if you avoid hard control in its first 2 seconds.
::map jungle | Clear the jungle and gank with Charge.
## Mid game and teamfights
Engage with Charge and avoid control in the first 2 seconds, then use the ultimate in the middle of the enemy team. Before you go in, check which enemy heroes still have their hard control available. A tank with a ready stun can stop the Enrage; once that stun is spent, your Charge gives you control immunity for the rest of its duration and you can walk through the enemy frontline to the backline.
Cleaving Axe gives damage reduction and bursts of movement speed with each slash, so you can move with the enemy while channeling it. Follow the group of enemies rather than standing still, so the final wide slash hits as many as possible.
## Advanced techniques
- Enrage timing: start Charge when the enemy's control is on cooldown.
- Skill weaving: each skill hit adds 2 seconds of enhanced attacks, up to 4 seconds stored, so cast skills before the enhanced state runs out.
- Ultimate positioning: use it in the middle of enemies for the wide slash.
- Second cast of The Power of Axe: the dash can be used even when the first swing missed, which makes it a reliable gap closer or escape.
- Slow removal: Charge removes slows, so save it for when the enemy kites you with slows.
## Draft and team fit
Aulus was the most picked fighter of the MPL PH S18 playoffs: 20 picks (12 wins) and 8 bans in 38 games. His most frequent partners there were Marcel (7 games together, 5 wins), Zhuxin (6 games, 3 wins), Kimmy and Nolan (4 games each, 3 wins each). In the MPL ID S18 playoffs, he was picked 18 times (7 wins) and banned 10 times. He pairs well with heroes who hold enemies in place, since his ultimate needs enemies to stay near him.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Sun | bad=Gloo,Tigreal,Minsitthar,Natalia,Ruby | ally=Estes,Angela,Atlas,Tigreal
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment.
Playing against Aulus: control him in the first 2 seconds of Charge; kite him. Once he is Enraged, back off and wait for the effect to end rather than wasting control skills on an immune target.
## Situational adjustments
- Against heavy control: build more defense.
- Against burst: build more HP.
- When ahead: invade the jungle.
## Practice drills
- Enrage drill: practice avoiding control during Charge.
- Weave drill: practice weaving skills and attacks.
## Common mistakes
- Engaging into control.
- Wasting the ultimate.
- Not weaving skills.

guides.title: Hilda
guides.sub: Bush fighter who stacks marks, then cuts a share of max HP off the target
guides.body:
## Identity: what Hilda is and why she is picked
Hilda is a melee physical fighter and tank who can roam or play the EXP lane. Her passive, **Blessing of Wilderness**, heals her 2% HP per second while she stands in a bush, and entering a bush enhances her next basic attack: it slows the target by 40% and also hits enemies behind it, then goes on a 6-second cooldown. Every basic attack and skill also applies a Wilderness Mark that lasts up to 4 seconds and stacks up to 6 times; each stack lowers the target's physical and magic defense by 3%.
**Combat Ritual** gives 60% movement speed and a shield worth 10% of her max HP for 3 seconds. **Art of Hunting** locks onto a target and can be cast up to 3 times: the second hit also damages enemies around the target, and the third knocks the target and nearby enemies back. Her ultimate, **Power of Wildness**, leaps onto the target for heavy damage and a 0.2-second stun, with nearby enemies taking 60% of it. Each Wilderness Mark adds 2.5% of the target's max HP as extra damage, and at max stacks the bonus is 20% of their max HP.
Why she is picked: she is very strong in early skirmishes around bushes, and her ultimate punishes tanky targets that other heroes cannot burst. Her weakness: outside bushes she has no sustain, and her engage tool is only a speed boost, so kiting heroes and long-range control frustrate her.
## Kit deep-dive
### Blessing of Wilderness (passive)
Two jobs: bush sustain and the mark stacks. Lane near bushes when you can, and open trades from a bush so the enhanced attack lands.
### Combat Ritual (Skill 1)
Your engage and escape. The shield is based on max HP, so it grows as you buy HP items.
### Art of Hunting (Skill 2)
Targeted, three casts, and the main source of mark stacks along with basic attacks. Save the third cast's knock-back to stop an escape or to push an enemy toward your team.
### Power of Wildness (Ultimate)
It deals the most damage at full stacks. Count your hits: a basic attack plus three Art of Hunting casts and a couple more attacks bring most targets close to max stacks.
::curve 5,4,3 | Very strong early around bushes, strong in mid-game skirmishes, and less decisive late when teams group and kite.
## Combos
::combo Bush opener | BA > S2 > S2 > BA > S2 > ULT | Enhanced attack from the bush, then stack marks with Art of Hunting and attacks, and finish with the ultimate.
::combo Engage | S1 > BA > S2 > S2 > S2 > ULT | Speed and shield to reach the target, then stack and finish.
## Builds and emblems
::build Fighter roam | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, War Axe, Brute Force Breastplate, Queen's Wings, Immortality | Damage and HP; the shield from Combat Ritual scales with max HP.
::build Tank roam | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Oracle, Immortality | For games where your team needs a frontline more than damage.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing on skill damage.
::spells Flicker, Petrify | Flicker for engage, Petrify to lock a target while you stack marks.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Hilda is one of the strongest early heroes in skirmishes around bushes. As a roamer, use river bushes to ambush the enemy jungler or roamer at the first buffs. In the EXP lane, stand in the lane bush between waves to heal.
::map roam | Ambush from river bushes around the first buffs and turtle.
## Mid game and teamfights
Pick the target you can fully stack: often the enemy fighter or tank who is at the front. The max-HP damage makes her ultimate dangerous for tanks. Avoid chasing ranged carries through open ground without your team.
## Advanced techniques
- Bush reset: after the enhanced attack goes on its 6-second cooldown, stepping back into a bush when it is ready gives you another one.
- Stack timing: the marks last 4 seconds, so do not pause between hits.
- Knock-back direction: aim the third Art of Hunting so it pushes the enemy toward your team or into a wall.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Tigreal,Franco,Belerick,Hylos | bad=Helcurt,Granger,Yin,Harley,Novaria | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Claude,Moskov
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: high-HP tanks lose the most to her max-HP ultimate.
Playing against Hilda: avoid fighting her near bushes, kite her, and do not let her keep hitting you for full stacks.
## Situational adjustments
- Against kiting teams: buy movement and save Combat Ritual to reach targets.
- Against tanks: max stacks plus the ultimate is your answer, so stay in fights longer.
- When ahead: invade the enemy jungle bushes with your jungler.
## Practice drills
- Stack drill: count to six marks on a training dummy before using the ultimate.
- Bush drill: practice stepping into a bush to refresh the enhanced attack.
## Common mistakes
- Using the ultimate with few stacks.
- Fighting in open lanes away from bushes.
- Chasing kiting heroes with no follow-up.

guides.title: Zhuxin
guides.sub: Lantern mage who stacks snares, captures enemies and throws them where she wants
guides.body:
## Identity: what Zhuxin is and why she is picked
Zhuxin is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane built around a channel. Her passive, **Crimson Butterflies**, turns the mana spent while channeling Lantern Flare into up to 15 butterflies; after the channel stops, each restores 3% of her max mana. She has a high base max mana that does not scale with level, so mana management is part of her skill.
**Fluttering Grace** hits a fan, applies a stack of Soul Snare, slows heroes hit by 20%-40% and gives her the same amount of movement speed for 1.5 seconds. **Lantern Flare** is held: she moves the Spirit Lantern with the skill button, damaging enemies in range every 0.33 seconds, applying Soul Snare and consuming 90 mana per tick. When a hero reaches 10 stacks, the butterflies capture them and pull them airborne for 1 second; releasing the skill throws the captured enemies to a target location for damage plus a share of max HP. Her ultimate, **Crimson Beacon**, blinks her to a location with a shield and creates a field for 6 seconds that applies Soul Snare every 0.5 seconds.
Why she is picked: a captured enemy can be thrown into your team, under your turret or away from their carry, which is a unique kind of control. Her weakness: she must channel near enemies, and mana runs out if she holds the lantern too long.
## Kit deep-dive
### Crimson Butterflies (passive)
Mana goes into butterflies while channeling and comes back afterwards. Release the channel in time to get the mana back.
### Fluttering Grace (Skill 1)
The slow and speed help you keep distance while channeling, and the snare stack counts toward a capture.
### Lantern Flare (Skill 2)
Your damage, stacks and capture. Move the lantern over the target rather than your own body, then release to throw.
### Crimson Beacon (Ultimate)
A blink with a shield and a stacking field. Use it to reach a group and stack Soul Snare on several heroes at once.
::curve 3,5,4 | Moderate early, strongest in mid-game objective fights and still valuable late as a control mage.
## Combos
::combo Capture and throw | S1 > S2 > S2 | Slow with the fan, channel the lantern to 10 stacks, then release to throw.
::combo Group capture | ULT > S1 > S2 > S2 | Blink in for the field, slow the group, channel and throw.
## Builds and emblems
::build Control mage | Arcane Boots, Enchanted Talisman, Clock of Destiny, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive | Enchanted Talisman's mana regen and Clock of Destiny's mana support a channel-heavy kit.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst after repeated hits.
::spells Flicker | Flicker lets you reposition while channeling.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Lantern Flare clears waves well, but each tick costs mana. Clear the wave efficiently, release the channel, and let the butterflies refund mana before the next wave.
::map rotate | Clear mid, then rotate to help with turtle and side-lane fights.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stand behind your frontline and channel on the enemy frontline or anyone in range. A captured enemy can be thrown into your team, which turns a fight. Choose the throw target before you start channeling.
## Advanced techniques
- Throw direction: under your turret, into your team, or away from the enemy carry.
- Mana budget: release the channel before running out so the butterflies refund mana.
- Ultimate entry: the field stacks snares on several heroes, so a well-placed ultimate can lead to multiple captures.
## Draft and team fit
Zhuxin is a pro-favored pick far more than a ranked one. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 17 times (9 wins) and banned 9 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, 22 picks (11 wins) and 13 bans. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, she is picked in only 0.39% of games, with a 50.77% win rate. Her pro partners show what she needs: frontliners and fighters such as Aulus, Atlas and Barats who keep enemies in her lantern, and junglers such as Hirara who follow up on a thrown target.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Barats | bad=Lolita,Khufra,Gloo,Hylos,Lukas | ally=Atlas,Aulus,Tigreal,Franco
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The ally list includes Aulus, her most frequent MPL PH S18 playoff partner (6 games together). The good list is an assessment: melee fighters must walk into her lantern.
Playing against Zhuxin: interrupt her channel, dive her before she captures, and do not stand in the lantern.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: keep Fluttering Grace for self-peel.
- Against heavy magic defense: Divine Glaive earlier.
- When ahead: control objectives by throwing enemies away from them.
## Practice drills
- Lantern drill: move the lantern over a moving dummy and count stacks.
- Throw drill: practice throwing a captured target to a chosen spot.
## Common mistakes
- Channeling until mana runs out.
- Standing in front of the frontline.
- Throwing enemies away from your team.

guides.title: Carmilla
guides.sub: Vampire support who links enemies so one stun hits all of them
guides.body:
## Identity: what Carmilla is and why she is picked
Carmilla is a melee magic support and tank for the roam. Her passive, **Vampire Pact**, steals physical and magic defense from enemy heroes she damages, stacking up to 5 times for 5 seconds, once per enemy every 5 seconds. **Crimson Flower** circles two flowers around her for 5 seconds, damaging and slowing enemies they hit (the slow stacks up to 50%) and healing her each time they deal damage. **Bloodbath** gives 70% movement speed that decays over 4.5 seconds; recast to unleash the stored energy on a target for damage and a stun of up to 0.6 seconds, scaling with how long she accumulated.
Her ultimate, **Curse of Blood**, slows enemies in an area by 50%; after 0.8 seconds, those still inside take damage, are immobilized for 1 second, and are linked for 5 seconds. While linked, damage or control on one spreads 50% of the damage and 100% of the control duration to every other linked target. With Cecilion on her team, she can also attach to him as a shield and then charge out with resets on her skills.
Why she is picked: a good Curse of Blood turns any single-target stun from your team into a team-wide stun. Her weakness: the link breaks when enemies move apart, and the ultimate has a long cooldown.
## Kit deep-dive
### Vampire Pact (passive)
Defense stolen from enemies makes her tankier the more she fights. Hit different enemies to steal from each of them.
### Crimson Flower (Skill 1)
Sustain and slow. Stay close to enemies so the flowers keep hitting.
### Bloodbath (Skill 2)
Your engage and your stun. Hold the accumulation longer for a stronger stun, or recast early to stop an enemy at once.
### Curse of Blood (Ultimate)
Cast it where enemies are grouped or forced to stand together, such as a turtle pit or a narrow path.
::curve 3,5,4 | Moderate early, strongest in mid-game objective fights and still useful late.
## Combos
::combo Link and stun | ULT > S2 | Curse a group, then stun one linked target to stun all of them.
::combo Roam engage | S2 > S1 > S2 | Speed in, flowers on, then recast the stun.
## Builds and emblems
::build Support tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Oracle, Immortality | Defense and healing for the frontline.
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Agility, Pull Yourself Together, Focusing Mark | Speed and a mark that boosts your team's damage on targets you hit.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for a better curse position.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Roam with your jungler and marksman. Bloodbath's speed lets you reach fights first.
::map roam | Roam between gold lane and mid.
## Mid game and teamfights
Find the moment enemies group, curse them, then let your team's control spread to all linked targets. Coordinate with your team before casting.
The curse has a short delay: enemies are slowed by 50% first, and only those still inside after 0.8 seconds are immobilized and linked. Cast it where enemies cannot easily walk out, such as the turtle or lord pit, a jungle entrance, or right after a teammate's area control. Once the link is active, call for your team's strongest single-target control on the most valuable linked hero: every other linked hero gets the same control.
## Advanced techniques
- Link value: any control on a linked target spreads at full duration, so pair her with heroes who have area or targeted control.
- Bloodbath timing: accumulation increases damage and stun duration.
- Defense theft: stealing from several enemies makes her very hard to kill.
## Draft and team fit
Carmilla needs teammates with control to spread through her link: any single-target stun or immobilize becomes a team-wide one. She has a joint skill with Cecilion, which makes that pair a natural duo. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 4 times without a win and banned 8 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs she was picked 9 times (4 wins) and banned 5 times. In ranked Mythical Glory+, she is banned in 38.24% of games, a sign that solo-queue players find the link hard to play against.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Aulus | bad=Popol and Kupa,Chip,Estes,Minotaur,Cyclops | ally=Cecilion,Atlas,Eudora,Pharsa
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Cecilion is in the ally list because of their joint skill. The good list is an assessment: melee fighters stay grouped and get linked.
Playing against Carmilla: move apart after the curse to break the link.
## Situational adjustments
- Against spread-out teams: use Bloodbath on single targets instead.
- Against healers: Dominance Ice for anti-heal.
- When ahead: control objectives and wait for enemies to group.
## Practice drills
- Link drill: curse grouped dummies and test how control spreads.
- Accumulation drill: practice holding Bloodbath for the strongest stun.
## Common mistakes
- Cursing a single enemy.
- Using the ultimate without team follow-up.
- Recasting Bloodbath too early.

guides.title: Nana
guides.sub: Beginner-friendly mage whose transformation and stuns punish groups
guides.body:
## Identity: what Nana is and why she is picked
Nana is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane, known as a beginner hero but still useful at higher ranks. Her passive, **Molina's Gift**, triggers on fatal damage: she removes debuffs, becomes untargetable and invincible for 2 seconds with 30% movement speed, and heals 10% of her max HP. It can trigger once every 150 seconds, and she cannot cast skills while transformed.
**Magic Boomerang** damages enemies on the way out and back; the damage drops by 20% for each additional enemy hit, up to 60%. **Molina Smooch** summons Molina, who chases the nearest enemy hero for 2.5 seconds and transforms the first one she touches for 1.5 seconds, slowing them by 50% and reducing their magic defense by 25%. Her ultimate, **Molina Blitz**, strikes an area 3 times, slowing enemies, and stuns enemies hit consecutively for 1 second.
Why she is picked: an area stun and a transform that stops a diver are easy to use and effective. Her weakness: short range and few escapes apart from her passive.
## Kit deep-dive
### Molina's Gift (passive)
A second chance. After it triggers, play carefully until it is back.
### Magic Boomerang (Skill 1)
Poke and wave clear. It hits on the way back too, so position so it passes through targets twice.
### Molina Smooch (Skill 2)
A transform that disables a hero; use it on divers or to start a kill.
### Molina Blitz (Ultimate)
Three strikes; enemies who stay in the area are stunned.
::curve 4,4,3 | Solid early and mid, less decisive late against magic defense.
## Combos
::combo Transform and stun | S2 > ULT > S1 | Transform the target so they cannot escape the ultimate's strikes.
::combo Poke | S1 > S1 | Boomerang out and back.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Lightning Truncheon, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Blood Wings | Damage, penetration and a shield.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst after repeated hits.
::spells Flicker | Flicker is the standard.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Poke the enemy mage with the boomerang and clear the wave quickly. Each additional enemy hit lowers the boomerang's damage, so against a single laner, aim to hit them alone rather than through the minions. Once you have your ultimate, rotate to side lanes where an enemy is pushing: Molina Smooch plus Molina Blitz is enough to secure kills with a teammate.
::map rotate | Clear mid and rotate to side lanes.
## Mid game and teamfights
Use Molina Smooch on the enemy diver, then ultimate grouped enemies.
Your role in fights depends on the enemy draft. Against assassins and divers, stay behind your frontline and keep Molina Smooch for the first hero who jumps on you or your marksman: a transformed enemy is slowed by 50% and cannot use their skills properly for 1.5 seconds.
