Against slower teams, use Smooch to start the fight on a frontliner and follow with the ultimate. The ultimate's stun only lands on enemies hit by consecutive strikes, so cast it where enemies are already slowed, transformed or locked by a teammate.
After your passive triggers, you have 2 seconds of invincibility and extra speed: use them to walk back to your team, not to stay in the fight, since you cannot cast skills while transformed.
## Advanced techniques
- Boomerang return: position so the boomerang hits on the way back.
- Smooch targeting: Molina chases the nearest hero, so place her close to your intended target.
- Passive awareness: track the 150-second cooldown.
## Draft and team fit
Nana suits teams that need reliable control without a difficult mechanical hero. She pairs well with tanks who group enemies, such as Atlas or Tigreal, because a grouped team is easier to hit with consecutive Molina Blitz strikes. Draft her when the enemy has several divers: Molina Smooch shuts one of them down for 1.5 seconds. Avoid her into heavy poke compositions that keep her out of her short range.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Fanny,Ling,Lancelot,Gusion | bad=Odette,Lolita,Estes,Edith,Alucard | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Franco,Johnson
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: divers are stopped by the transform.
Playing against Nana: bait her passive, then kill her again.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: hold Smooch for defense.
- Against magic defense: Divine Glaive earlier.
- When ahead: control objectives with your ultimate.
- Against heroes who punish the passive: some heroes can wait out the 2-second invincibility. After it is used, play further back.
## Practice drills
- Boomerang drill: practice hitting on the way back, so one cast damages the same target twice.
- Smooch drill: practice placing Molina near the target.
## Common mistakes
- Wasting Smooch.
- Standing in front after the passive is used.
- Ignoring the passive cooldown.

guides.title: Alice
guides.sub: Blood mage who heals by standing in the middle of the enemy team
guides.body:
## Identity: what Alice is and why she is picked
Alice is a melee magic tank and mage for the EXP lane or jungle. Her passive, **Crimson Blood Banquet**, adds a stack of Crimson each time her skills hit; at 2 stacks, Blood Banquet activates for a few seconds, dealing a share of the target's max HP as magic damage to nearby units every 0.5 seconds, healing her 10 HP per tick and giving 8% movement speed. Hitting heroes with skills refreshes it.
**Crimson Gleam** fires blood energy forward; recast before it dissipates to blink to it. **Doom Waltz** has a short cooldown, damages nearby enemies, slows them by 70% for 1 second, and while Blood Banquet is active deals 300% of its damage and heals her for the same amount. Her ultimate, **Throne of Ruin**, gives control immunity and 50% damage reduction while slowing her by 50%; after 1.5 seconds she descends, damaging and immobilizing enemies for 1 second.
Why she is picked: she is a frontliner with strong sustain and an area immobilize that cannot be interrupted by control. Her weakness: she must be in melee range for everything.
## Kit deep-dive
### Crimson Blood Banquet (passive)
Two skill hits start the aura. Keep it active with skills on heroes.
### Crimson Gleam (Skill 1)
Engage and escape: fire, then blink.
### Doom Waltz (Skill 2)
Her main sustain and slow, with a short cooldown.
### Throne of Ruin (Ultimate)
Control immunity during the charge, then an area immobilize.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, strong mid and very durable late.
## Combos
::combo Blink engage | S1 > S1 > S2 > ULT | Fire and blink in, Waltz to start the Banquet, then the ultimate.
::combo Sustain loop | S2 > BA > S2 | Waltz repeatedly while the Banquet is active.
## Builds and emblems
::build Sustain mage-tank | Tough Boots, Clock of Destiny, Concentrated Energy, Radiant Armor, Antique Cuirass, Immortality | HP, magic power and defense.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing.
::spells Flicker, Retribution | Flicker for engages; Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Trade with Doom Waltz once the Banquet is active. In the jungle, Blood Banquet's damage against creeps is capped (70 plus 10 per hero level), so her clear relies on Doom Waltz and basic attacks more than on the aura.
In the EXP lane, the best trades start with Crimson Gleam to land the first stack, then a blink and Doom Waltz for the second stack, which starts the Banquet. From there, Doom Waltz deals triple damage and heals for the same amount, so a trade that lasts several seconds swings in your favor. Back off when Doom Waltz is on cooldown and the enemy laner still has their burst.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane with sustain trades.
## Mid game and teamfights
Blink into the enemy team, start the Banquet, Waltz repeatedly and use the ultimate for an area immobilize.
Your job is to stand where the enemy does not want you: on top of their backline or between their carry and their frontline. The aura damages every nearby unit and heals you each tick, so the more enemies around you, the more you heal. Use the ultimate when several enemies are close: during its 1.5-second charge you are immune to control and take 50% less damage, so it doubles as a way to survive the enemy's response. While charging you can still use Scarlet Shadow, the recast of Crimson Gleam, to move the landing spot onto the enemy carry.
## Advanced techniques
- Banquet refresh: hitting heroes with skills refreshes the aura.
- Ultimate blink: during the charge, Scarlet Shadow (the Crimson Gleam recast) is the only skill you can use, so fire Crimson Gleam just before the ultimate to keep the blink available.
- Waltz healing: the heal scales with the Banquet's damage.
## Draft and team fit
Alice was a strong pro pick in Indonesia: in the MPL ID S18 playoffs she was picked 14 times (8 wins) and banned 17 times, often with Cici (6 games together), Gloo (5 games, 4 wins) and Kimmy (5 games, 3 wins). In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 7 times (2 wins) and banned 9 times. She suits teams that want a frontliner who can survive inside the enemy team, especially against compositions without much anti-heal.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Cici,Masha,Freya,Paquito | bad=Faramis,Chip,Popol and Kupa,Phoveus,Barats | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Pharsa,Eudora
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Alice is in the official counter list for Cici, which is the basis of part of the good list; the rest is an assessment from her sustain.
Playing against Alice: anti-heal and kiting. Do not group around her when the Banquet is active, and save your control for after her ultimate, when she is no longer immune.
## Situational adjustments
- Against anti-heal: more HP.
- Against kiting: Flicker for engages.
- When ahead: dive the backline.
## Practice drills
- Banquet drill: practice two skill hits to start the aura.
- Blink drill: practice Crimson Gleam blinks.
## Common mistakes
- Fighting without the Banquet.
- Blinking into the enemy without follow-up.
- Wasting the ultimate.

guides.title: Miya
guides.sub: Classic hyper-carry marksman whose attack speed snowballs into a storm of arrows
guides.body:
## Identity: what Miya is and why she is picked
Miya is a ranged physical marksman for the gold lane and one of the first heroes most players learn. Do not let that fool you: at high ranks she is a late-game carry whose damage keeps climbing as long as she can keep attacking. Her passive, **Moon Blessing**, gives 5% attack speed for 4 seconds each time she hits a target, stacking 5 times. At full stacks, every basic attack also summons a Moonlight Shadow that deals 30 physical damage and inherits a portion of attack effects.
**Moon Arrow** makes each basic attack fire two extra arrows for 4 seconds, dealing 10-35 physical damage to the target and 30% damage to nearby targets; each arrow inherits a portion of attack effects. **Arrow of Eclipse** hits an area for 270-420 physical damage, immobilizes enemies inside for 1.2 seconds, then splits into 6 minor arrows that each deal 40-105 damage to the first enemy hit and slow by 30% for 2 seconds. Her ultimate, **Hidden Moonlight**, removes all debuffs, conceals her and gives 65% extra movement speed for 2 seconds or until she attacks; she leaves it with full Moon Blessing stacks.
Why she is picked: very high sustained damage with attack-effect items, an area immobilize, and an ultimate that is both a cleanse and an escape. Her weakness: she has no dash, so a single well-timed engage after her ultimate is used can kill her.
## Kit deep-dive
### Moon Blessing (passive)
Full stacks are where her damage starts. Keep attacking, and remember that leaving Hidden Moonlight gives full stacks at once.
### Moon Arrow (Skill 1)
Three projectiles per attack, all inheriting a portion of attack effects. It also clears waves and jungle camps quickly thanks to the splash to nearby targets.
### Arrow of Eclipse (Skill 2)
Your only control: a 1.2-second immobilize on an area, plus slowing arrows. Use it to stop a diver or to keep a fleeing target in range.
### Hidden Moonlight (Ultimate)
A cleanse, concealment and speed boost in one. Its most important use is removing a stun or slow that would otherwise get you killed.
::curve 2,4,5 | Weak early, strong mid game once she has attack speed and attack effects, and one of the strongest damage dealers late.
## Combos
::combo Full damage | S1 > BA > S2 > BA | Moon Arrow for extra arrows, attack, immobilize with Arrow of Eclipse, keep attacking.
::combo Escape and reset | ULT > BA > S2 | Cleanse and conceal, walk to safety, then come out of concealment with full stacks and immobilize the chaser.
::combo Diver answer | S2 > S1 > BA | Immobilize the assassin who jumped on you, then turn and shoot.
## Builds and emblems
::build Attack-speed carry | Swift Boots, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword, Golden Staff, Haas' Claws, Wind of Nature | Attack effects stack through her extra arrows and Moonlight Shadows; Wind of Nature blocks physical burst.
::build Crit option (test it) | Swift Boots, Berserker's Fury, Windtalker, Haas' Claws, Malefic Roar, Wind of Nature | More burst per arrow instead of on-hit effects.
::emblem Custom Marksman Emblem | Fatal, Weapon Master, Weakness Finder | Crit and attack, more value from items and a slow on attacks.
::spells Flicker, Inspire | Flicker gives the dash she lacks; Inspire increases damage in extended fights.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Miya is weak in the first minutes. Farm the gold lane, last-hit carefully and avoid long trades with marksmen who have stronger early skills. Moon Arrow clears the wave quickly, which lets you push and then stand back near your turret. Your goal is to reach your first two attack-effect items without dying.
::map lane | Farm the gold lane safely and push with Moon Arrow.
## Mid game and teamfights
Once you have two or three items, Miya becomes a threat. Stay behind your tank and hit whatever is closest and safe to hit. Use Arrow of Eclipse on the enemy hero who dives toward you, not on the frontline at the start. Hold Hidden Moonlight until an enemy has used control on you, then cleanse it and reposition.
## Advanced techniques
- Ultimate as a cleanse: it removes all debuffs, so it can break stuns, slows and marks. Save it rather than using it to chase.
- Full stacks on exit: leaving concealment gives full Moon Blessing, so re-enter fights straight into maximum damage.
- Positioning over mechanics: with no dash, her survival depends on standing behind a frontliner and outside the range of enemy engage.
- Splash damage: Moon Arrow's extra arrows deal 30% to nearby targets, so grouped enemies take damage from every attack.
## Draft and team fit
Miya wants a team that protects her: a tank who peels, a support who heals or shields, and a fighter who holds the enemy divers. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, she is picked in 1.34% of games with a 50.24% win rate. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 3 times (1 win), so pro teams rarely chose her.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Belerick,Tigreal,Franco,Hylos | bad=Saber,Guinevere,Jawhead,Irithel,Obsidia | ally=Estes,Angela,Tigreal,Atlas
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: slow tanks who cannot reach her take her full sustained damage.
Playing against Miya: wait for her ultimate, then engage; assassins with targeted burst are the cleanest answer.
## Situational adjustments
- Against assassins: Wind of Nature or a defensive item earlier, and hold Arrow of Eclipse for defense.
- Against tanks: Demon Hunter Sword early.
- When behind: farm safely and wait for a fight where your frontline engages first.
## Practice drills
- Stacking drill: reach full Moon Blessing stacks quickly on a dummy.
- Cleanse drill: practice using the ultimate right after being stunned.
## Common mistakes
- Using the ultimate to chase.
- Standing in front of the frontline.
- Fighting before having items.

guides.title: Hanabi
guides.sub: Bouncing-blade marksman who becomes immune to control while shielded
guides.body:
## Identity: what Hanabi is and why she is picked
Hanabi is a ranged physical marksman for the gold lane whose damage spreads. Her passive, **Ninjutsu: Petal Barrage**, makes her basic attacks and skills launch Petal Blades after hitting a target, bouncing up to 4 times to nearby enemies: the first bounce deals 40% of the damage and each next one 85% of the previous. Bounces from basic attacks inherit a portion of attack effects.
**Ninjutsu: Equinox** has a passive and an active part. Passive: she is immune to control effects whenever she has a shield from any source. Active: a 300-600 shield for 5 seconds, plus 20% movement speed and 25% attack speed while it lasts, and 20% of the damage she deals is added to the shield (10% against non-hero units), up to 50% of her max HP. **Ninjutsu: Soul Scroll** throws a kunai for 450-600 physical damage that slows by 60% for 1 second and marks enemies, so her next bounce on them deals 30-180 physical damage with no decay. Her ultimate, **Forbidden Jutsu: Higanbana**, immobilizes the first enemy hero hit for 0.8 seconds and blooms after 1 second for area damage.
Why she is picked: in grouped fights, her bounces spread damage across the enemy team, and her shield makes her immune to control. Her weakness: no dash at all, and once the shield breaks she is easy to catch.
## Kit deep-dive
### Ninjutsu: Petal Barrage (passive)
Damage spreads to up to 4 nearby enemies. She is strongest when enemies stand close together.
### Ninjutsu: Equinox (Skill 1)
The key to her survival: as long as the shield holds, she cannot be controlled. Damage dealt feeds the shield.
### Ninjutsu: Soul Scroll (Skill 2)
Poke, slow and a mark that makes the next bounce stronger.
### Forbidden Jutsu: Higanbana (Ultimate)
A catch tool with an area follow-up.
::curve 2,4,5 | Weak early, strong mid and very strong late in grouped fights.
## Combos
::combo Shield and shoot | S1 > S2 > BA | Shield for immunity, mark with the kunai, then attack.
::combo Catch | ULT > S2 > BA | Immobilize, slow and mark, then attack.
## Builds and emblems
::build Bounce carry | Swift Boots, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword, Golden Staff, Haas' Claws, Wind of Nature | Bounces from basic attacks inherit attack effects.
::emblem Custom Marksman Emblem | Fatal, Weapon Master, Weakness Finder | Crit and attack, more value from items and a slow on attacks.
::spells Flicker | She has no dash, so Flicker is her escape.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Farm safely. Soul Scroll is your poke, and the shield protects you from early ganks.
Hanabi has no dash, so her early game is about not giving the enemy a reason to dive her. Use Soul Scroll on the wave and the enemy marksman together when they line up: the kunai hits everything along its path and slows by 60% for 1 second. When the enemy jungler shows up, activate Equinox before their control lands, since the shield makes you immune to control while it holds, then walk back to your turret with the extra 20% movement speed.
::map lane | Farm the gold lane.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stay behind the frontline. Cast the shield just before the enemy engages so their control does nothing. Attack the closest enemies and let the bounces hit the rest.
Her damage spreads, so she does the most work when enemies stand close together: around the turtle or lord, in a jungle entrance, or after a tank's area control. The shield grows by 20% of the damage she deals to heroes, capped at 50% of her max HP, so in a large fight it can keep refilling as long as she keeps hitting. Use Higanbana on the hero who threatens you most: the 0.8-second immobilize lets you shield and reposition, and the bloom after 1 second damages everyone near that target.
## Advanced techniques
- Shield timing: activate it right before the enemy's control lands.
- Any shield counts: shields from supports and items also give control immunity.
- Bounce positioning: attack enemies standing close to others.
- Soul Scroll marks: marked enemies take 30-180 extra bounce damage from your next basic attack with no decay, so throw the kunai through a group before attacking.
- Shield feeding: the shield takes only 10% of damage dealt to non-hero units, so in fights, hit heroes to keep it up.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Tigreal,Atlas,Franco,Kaja | bad=Popol and Kupa,Kaja,Saber,Akai,Kalea | ally=Estes,Angela,Mathilda,Diggie
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Note: Kaja appears in both lists. The good list is an assessment from her kit; the official data says Kaja wins the matchup in ranked, so treat it as a skill matchup.
Playing against Hanabi: break her shield first, then control her.
## Situational adjustments
- Against assassins: Wind of Nature earlier.
- Against tanks: Demon Hunter Sword earlier.
- When behind: farm safely.
## Practice drills
- Shield timing drill: practice shielding before control lands.
- Bounce drill: attack grouped dummies.
## Common mistakes
- Using the shield too early.
- Standing in front.
- Fighting alone.

guides.title: Angela
guides.sub: Puppet support who heals with every wave and rides on her carry as a living shield
guides.body:
## Identity: what Angela is and why she is picked
Angela is a ranged magic support for the roam. She keeps her team alive with constant heals and a shield that can reach anyone on the map, then attaches to an ally and keeps casting. Her passive, **Smart Heart**, gives 7.5% movement speed for 4 seconds each time she casts a skill, stacking up to 30%; when she is attached to an ally, that speed goes to them.
**Love Waves** fires waves that deal 170-320 magic damage, briefly reveal enemies and apply Lover's Mark (up to 5 stacks, each increasing the damage by 20% and slowing by 8% for 3 seconds), while restoring 150-200 HP to allies hit. She stores up to 5 charges. **Puppet-on-a-String** links a target enemy for 300-450 magic damage and slows them up to 80%; if they are still connected after 3 seconds, they are immobilized for 1.5 seconds and take 450-675 magic damage, increased by 20% per Lover's Mark. Her ultimate, **Heartguard**, channels for 2 seconds to give a 1000-2000 shield to any allied hero regardless of distance, then attaches her to that ally for 12 seconds, during which her skills cost no mana.
Why she is picked: a global shield that saves carries in fights she is not even near, steady healing, and a reliable immobilize. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she is picked in 2.01% of games and banned in 9.48%, with a 50.25% win rate. Her weakness: she is fragile and her shield needs a 2-second channel.
## Kit deep-dive
### Smart Heart (passive)
Every cast adds speed. While attached, your ally gets it, which helps them chase or escape.
### Love Waves (Skill 1)
Five charges and a 2-second recharge. It heals allies and stacks marks on enemies at the same time.
### Puppet-on-a-String (Skill 2)
A 3-second tether that ends in a 1.5-second immobilize. Stay within range so the string holds.
### Heartguard (Ultimate)
The big save. Start the channel before the enemy bursts your carry, not after.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, solid mid and very strong late when her shield protects fed carries.
## Combos
::combo Mark and bind | S1 > S1 > S2 > S1 | Stack Lover's Mark with waves, attach the string, keep waving until it immobilizes.
::combo Save and attach | ULT > S1 > S1 > S2 | Shield the ally, attach, then cast waves and the string at no mana cost.
## Builds and emblems
::build Healer support | Magic Shoes, Enchanted Talisman, Fleeting Time, Flask of the Oasis, Oracle, Immortality | Mana and cooldowns for constant waves, stronger heals and shields, and survival.
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Agility, Pull Yourself Together, Focusing Mark | Speed, lower spell cooldowns and a damage mark for your team.
::spells Flicker, Revitalize | Flicker for safety; Revitalize adds more healing.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Stay with your marksman or jungler, heal them through trades with Love Waves, and look for strings on enemies who walk too close. Each wave also briefly reveals enemies, which helps you check bushes.
::map roam | Support the gold lane early, then follow your jungler to objectives.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stand behind your team and spread heals with Love Waves. When an enemy dives your carry, start Heartguard immediately: the shield lands after the channel starts, and then you are attached. Attaching to a frontliner lets you heal and string from inside the fight.
## Advanced techniques
- Global shield: Heartguard works at any distance, so you can save a teammate in another lane.
- Attach target: attach to whoever will survive the fight longest; if that ally dies, the attach ends.
- Free spam: while attached, your skills cost no mana, so cast waves constantly.
- Puppet range: stay close after attaching the string; if the enemy walks out of range, there is no immobilize.
## Draft and team fit
Angela is at her best with a carry who can make use of a big shield and constant heals: hypercarry marksmen such as Miya or Layla, or a jungler who dives and needs to come out alive. She is also a safe pick when your team has no other way to save a carry from burst. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, she is picked in 2.01% of games, more than most supports, with a 50.25% win rate. She did not appear in the MPL PH or MPL ID Season 18 playoff stats.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Lesley,Miya,Layla,Hanabi | bad=Marcel,Alice,Lancelot,Faramis,Balmond | ally=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Ling
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good and ally lists are assessments: immobile carries gain the most from her shield.
Playing against Angela: dive her first, or burst her ally before the channel finishes.
## Situational adjustments
- Against burst: hold the ultimate for your carry.
- Against healers: build anti-heal on your carry.
- When ahead: attach to your fighter and push.
## Practice drills
- Wave drill: hit allies and enemies with the same wave.
- Shield timing drill: start the channel before the enemy engages.
## Common mistakes
- Waiting too long to shield.
- Attaching to an ally who is about to die.
- Missing the string immobilize.

guides.title: Kaja
guides.sub: Lightning support who snatches a target and drags them into his team
guides.body:
## Identity: what Kaja is and why he is picked
Kaja is a melee magic support for the roam built to catch one enemy and bring them to his team. His passive, **Wings of Lightning**, applies Paralysis with every skill: enemies are briefly slowed and deal 8% less damage for 5 seconds.
**Ring of Order** releases a ring that expands and returns, dealing 160-285 magic damage and healing him for 78-138 per enemy hit (subsequent hits heal 33%). **Soaring Wings** dashes to an area with control immunity during the dash, knocks back and stuns nearby enemies for 0.5 seconds, then puts him in the Soaring state for 6.6 seconds: he ignores obstacles, gains 15% movement speed, and attacks while moving. Hitting a hero or creep extends it by 2.6 seconds, and the skill's second cast has a 4-second cooldown. His ultimate, **Divine Binding**, throws a lasso: after 0.5 seconds, enemy heroes in the area take 360-600 magic damage and are trapped for 2.5 seconds, and he can drag the lasso, pulling enemies at its edge.
Why he is picked: his ultimate removes one or more enemies from the fight. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, he is banned in 22.41% of games despite a 0.92% pick rate. His weakness: once his ultimate is down, he has much less impact.
## Kit deep-dive
### Wings of Lightning (passive)
Every hit weakens the enemy's damage by 8%. Keep your skills landing.
### Ring of Order (Skill 1)
Damage and self-heal with a short cooldown.
### Soaring Wings (Skill 2)
Engage and mobility. The dash makes you immune to control.
### Divine Binding (Ultimate)
The catch. Drag trapped enemies toward your team.
::curve 4,5,4 | Strong picks early, very strong mid game and still decisive late.
## Combos
::combo Pick | S2 > ULT > S1 | Dash in, trap and drag, then ring.
::combo Flicker catch | Flicker > ULT > S1 | Flicker into range, trap, ring.
## Builds and emblems
::build Roam tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Oracle, Immortality | Durability for diving into the enemy backline.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP and defense.
::spells Flicker | Flicker extends the ultimate's reach.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Roam with your jungler and look for picks on isolated enemies.
Kaja's ultimate comes online at level 4, and from then on every enemy who walks alone is a target. Ring of Order heals him for each enemy hit, so he can trade in lane without backing. Soaring Wings is both his engage and his rotation tool: the Soaring state lets him ignore obstacles and fly over walls, and hitting a hero or creep keeps it going. Use it to arrive at a lane from an angle the enemy does not watch.
::map roam | Roam between lanes looking for picks.
## Mid game and teamfights
Target the enemy carry. Trap them and drag them into your team.
The lasso traps every enemy hero inside its area after a 0.5-second delay, so it can catch two heroes when they stand close together. Once they are trapped, drag the lasso toward your team: it shrinks and pulls enemies at the edge. Dragging does not interrupt their skills, so a trapped mage can still cast; the value is in moving them away from their team and into yours. Tell your team before you go in, because a dragged carry dies only if someone is there to hit them.
After the ultimate, your job changes: stay near your carry, use Ring of Order for damage and healing, and use Soaring Wings' knock-back and stun to stop divers.
## Advanced techniques
- Drag direction: toward your team or turret.
- Soaring: ignore obstacles to approach from unexpected angles. Your turn radius is restricted while soaring, so plan the path before you take off.
- Control immunity: the dash cannot be interrupted, so it is a safe way to start a fight into enemy control.
- Second dash: entering the Soaring state reduces Soaring Wings' cooldown to 4 seconds, which gives you a second engage or an exit.
- Paralysis: every skill hit reduces the enemy's damage by 8% for 5 seconds, so even a ring on the enemy carry helps your team survive.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Hanabi,Miya,Layla,Lesley | bad=Valir,Akai,Estes,Kimmy,Beatrix | ally=Ling,Lancelot,Gusion,Hayabusa
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Kaja is in the official counter list for Hanabi. The ally list is an assessment: burst assassins finish dragged targets.
Playing against Kaja: stay near your team and keep a cleanse or control ready. Watch for him flying over walls in the Soaring state, and do not walk alone through the river when his ultimate is up.
## Situational adjustments
- Against grouped teams: wait for isolated targets.
- Against heavy control: dash in after their skills.
- When ahead: invade with your jungler.
## Practice drills
- Lasso drill: practice dragging.
- Soaring drill: practice movement.
## Common mistakes
- Using the ultimate on a tank.
- Dragging away from your team.
- Engaging alone.

guides.title: Lesley
guides.sub: Sniper marksman who crits from range and finishes with four bullets
guides.body:
## Identity: what Lesley is and why she is picked
Lesley is a ranged physical marksman for the gold lane. Her passive, **Lethal Shot**, gives her next basic attack extra range, 50% crit chance and 100 true damage if she has not taken damage for 5 seconds. Physical penetration converts to crit damage, but her base crit damage is reduced to 130%. She uses energy instead of mana, restored by basic attacks.
**Master of Camouflage** gives 3 seconds of camouflage with double energy regen, 40% movement speed and 85-135 physical attack, ending when she deals or takes damage. **Tactical Grenade** knocks enemies back in a cone while she jumps back. Her ultimate, **Ultimate Snipe**, locks onto an enemy hero and fires 4 Lethal Bullets, each dealing 250-350 plus 5% of the enemy's lost HP.
Why she is picked: long range and burst. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she is picked in 1.71% of games with a 48.39% win rate. Her weakness: fragile and dependent on not taking damage.
## Kit deep-dive
### Lethal Shot (passive)
Avoid damage for 5 seconds for a long-range crit.
### Master of Camouflage (Skill 1)
Speed and attack for repositioning.
### Tactical Grenade (Skill 2)
Disengage and knock-back.
### Ultimate Snipe (Ultimate)
Four bullets that finish low targets.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, strong mid and very strong late.
## Combos
::combo Snipe finish | BA > ULT > S2 | Lethal Shot, snipe, grenade to cancel the last bullet early.
::combo Disengage | S2 > S1 > BA | Grenade away, camouflage, shoot.
## Builds and emblems
::build Crit sniper | Swift Boots, Berserker's Fury, Windtalker, Haas' Claws, Malefic Roar, Wind of Nature | Crit and penetration; penetration becomes crit damage for her.
::emblem Custom Marksman Emblem | Fatal, Weapon Master, Weakness Finder | Crit and attack.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Poke with Lethal Shot from range and farm.
Lesley's early game is about keeping Lethal Shot available: if she does not take damage for 5 seconds, her next attack gains extra range, 50% crit chance and 100 true damage. Stay at the edge of your range, hit the enemy marksman with Lethal Shot when it is ready, then step back. Using a skill also starts the passive's cooldown, so do not waste skills on the wave if you want to poke. She uses energy rather than mana: basic attacks restore 5 energy and Lethal Shot doubles it.
::map lane | Farm the gold lane.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stay far back and shoot from range. Use the ultimate on low targets.
Her ultimate locks onto an enemy hero and fires 4 Lethal Bullets, each dealing 250-350 plus 5% of the target's lost HP, so it deals the most to targets who are already hurt. Bullets can be blocked by other enemy heroes, so look for a clear line before you fire. If the ultimate is interrupted, each remaining bullet reduces its cooldown by 10%. Master of Camouflage gives 40% movement speed and 85-135 physical attack for up to 3 seconds; use it to reposition before a fight or to walk away from a diver, and remember that enemies can see the distortion it causes.
## Advanced techniques
- Penetration to crit: each point of fixed physical penetration and each 1% physical penetration becomes 1% crit damage, which is why penetration items are worth more on her than on other marksmen.
- Grenade cancel: casting Tactical Grenade during the ultimate cancels it and fires a Fatal Bullet at once, which also jumps you back.
- Lethal Shot reset: avoid damage for 5 seconds; the camouflage helps you get there safely.
- Vision: the ultimate gives vision of nearby enemies, which can help find a target hiding in a bush.
## Draft and team fit
Lesley needs a frontline that keeps divers off her and a team that can fight at range. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, she is picked in 1.71% of games with a 48.39% win rate. In the MPL ID S18 playoffs she was picked twice (2 wins) and banned 6 times; she did not appear in the MPL PH S18 playoff stats. Avoid her into drafts with several assassins unless your team has strong peel.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Angela | bad=Marcel,Bruno,Claude,Baxia,Gatotkaca | ally=Estes,Angela,Tigreal,Atlas
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Lesley: dive her. She has only a short jump back from Tactical Grenade, so heroes who reach her quickly, or who poke her to deny Lethal Shot, make her game hard.
## Situational adjustments
- Against assassins: Wind of Nature, and save Tactical Grenade to knock them back.
- Against tanks: Malefic Roar earlier for penetration, which also adds crit damage.
- When behind: farm and poke from range rather than joining risky fights.
## Practice drills
- Snipe drill: practice finishing low-HP targets with the ultimate and cancelling with the grenade.
- Lethal Shot drill: practice keeping the passive ready by staying out of damage.
## Common mistakes
- Taking poke damage that keeps Lethal Shot on cooldown.
- Using the ultimate on full-HP targets.
- Firing the ultimate through enemy heroes who block the bullets.

guides.title: Floryn
guides.sub: Lantern healer whose ultimate heals the whole team anywhere on the map
guides.body:
## Identity: what Floryn is and why she is picked
Floryn is a ranged magic support for the roam. Her passive, **Dew**, gives her a special Lantern that permanently increases her attributes; she never sells it. After 5 seconds out of combat she can share a Flower of Hope with an ally (30-second cooldown), which gives that ally a 100 shield each time Floryn heals them.
**Sow** hits a target enemy for 180-330 magic damage, then Healing Fruits bounce to nearby allies, restoring 175-225 HP. **Sprout** explodes on the first enemy hit for 175-350 magic damage and stuns nearby enemies for 0.5 seconds. Her ultimate, **Bloom**, heals all allied heroes for 250-450 HP 2 times, no matter where they are, and boosts their shields and HP regen by 12% for 2 seconds.
Why she is picked: a global team heal. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she has a 53.89% win rate and a 12.56% ban rate. Her weakness: fragile, with modest control.
## Kit deep-dive
### Dew (passive)
Share the Flower of Hope with your carry for extra shields.
### Sow (Skill 1)
Poke and heal.
### Sprout (Skill 2)
A short stun.
### Bloom (Ultimate)
The global heal.
::curve 3,4,4 | Solid throughout.
## Combos
::combo Poke and heal | S1 > S2 | Sow for the heal, then Sprout.
## Builds and emblems
::build Healer | Magic Shoes, Enchanted Talisman, Fleeting Time, Flask of the Oasis, Oracle, Immortality | Healing and cooldowns.
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Agility, Pull Yourself Together, Focusing Mark | Speed and cooldowns.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Support your marksman with heals.
Sow is your main tool: it damages the target enemy, then Healing Fruits bounce to nearby allies for 175-225 HP. Use it on the enemy marksman while your own marksman is next to you, so you trade and heal at once. Before fights, step out of combat for 5 seconds and share the Flower of Hope with your carry: every time you heal them afterwards, they also gain a 100 shield. Sprout's 0.5-second stun is short, but it can stop a dash or set up your jungler's gank.
::map roam | Roam with your marksman.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stay behind and heal. Save Bloom for when several allies are low.
Bloom heals every allied hero twice, wherever they are, and briefly boosts shields and HP regen by 12%. That makes it the strongest answer to a long fight around an objective, and it can also save a teammate in another lane. The common mistake is to use it at the start of a fight; wait until the enemy has spent its burst and several allies are hurt. Stay behind your frontline, keep Sow on cooldown, and use Sprout to stop divers who reach you.
## Advanced techniques
- Global heal: Bloom reaches allies anywhere, so watch the minimap for a teammate in trouble in another lane.
- Flower of Hope: share it before fights; it needs 5 seconds out of combat and has a 30-second cooldown.
- Lantern: the Lantern from her passive permanently raises her attributes and cannot be sold, so plan your other five item slots around it.
- Sow targeting: Sow needs an enemy target, so you heal allies by hitting enemies near them.
## Draft and team fit
Floryn fits teams that want to win long fights: a durable frontline, fighters who stay in combat, and a carry who benefits from the Flower of Hope's shields. Her ranked numbers over the past 7 days in Mythical Glory+ are among the best of any support: a 53.89% win rate with a 1.28% pick rate and a 12.56% ban rate. She did not appear in the MPL PH or MPL ID Season 18 playoff stats. The official counter list (Marcel, Alice, X.Borg, Faramis and Ling) mixes heroes who dive the backline with heroes who win extended fights on their own, so draft extra protection when the enemy has them.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Lesley,Miya,Layla,Hanabi | bad=Marcel,Alice,X.Borg,Faramis,Ling | ally=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Lesley
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Floryn: anti-heal and dive. She has no escape skill, so heroes who reach the backline quickly can kill her before she uses Bloom.
## Situational adjustments
- Against anti-heal: focus on shields from the Flower of Hope and Oracle.
- Against divers: keep Sprout for defense and stay close to your tank.
- When ahead: rotate with your team and keep Bloom for objective fights.
## Practice drills
- Heal drill: hit enemies near allies so the Healing Fruits reach them.
- Bloom timing drill: in practice games, wait until two or more allies are low before using Bloom.
## Common mistakes
- Using Bloom too early.
- Forgetting to share the Flower of Hope before fights.
- Standing in front of the frontline.

guides.title: Tigreal
guides.sub: Hammer tank whose Implosion pulls a whole team into one stun
guides.body:
## Identity: what Tigreal is and why he is picked
Tigreal is a melee physical tank for the roam and a classic first tank for new players, but his engage remains among the most powerful in the game. His passive, **Fearless**, gives a stack each time he casts a skill or is hit by a basic attack; at 4 stacks, he blocks the next basic attack, including a turret shot. Minion attacks do not count.
**Attack Wave** sends a shockwave forward that erupts 3 times for 270-520 physical damage each, slowing by 20%, 40% and then 60% for 1.5 seconds. **Sacred Hammer** charges forward, pushing enemies along to the end of the charge; recast within 4 seconds to knock enemies in front of him airborne for 1 second. His ultimate, **Implosion**, stuns and pulls nearby enemies to him for 2 seconds and deals 600-1000 physical damage. The first half of the channel can be interrupted by control; the second half only by suppression.
Why he is picked: one well-placed combo can stun most of the enemy team at once. His weakness: he is slow, and his engage is predictable if he walks in without cover. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, his win rate is 43.86%, among the lowest of the popular tanks, which says his engage is easy to see coming in high-rank solo queue.
## Kit deep-dive
### Fearless (passive)
Blocks a basic attack every 4 stacks. Useful for tower dives.
### Attack Wave (Skill 1)
Three eruptions with growing slows. Use it to slow enemies before engaging.
### Sacred Hammer (Skill 2)
The charge pushes enemies; the recast knocks them airborne.
### Implosion (Ultimate)
The big pull. Only the second half is safe from regular control.
::curve 3,5,4 | Moderate early, strongest in mid-game objective fights and still decisive late.
## Combos
::combo Classic engage | S2 > ULT > S2 | Charge pushes enemies together, Implosion pulls and stuns, recast knocks airborne.
::combo Flicker Implosion | ULT > Flicker | Start Implosion, then Flicker into the group so the pull catches them.
::combo Slow and charge | S1 > S2 > S2 | Slow with the wave, then charge and knock airborne.
## Builds and emblems
::build Engage tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Guardian Helmet, Immortality | Defense, anti-heal and regeneration to survive the engage.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP and defense.
::spells Flicker | Flicker gives the surprise range his engage lacks.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Roam with your marksman and jungler. Tigreal's slows and knock-ups set up kills, and Fearless blocks a turret shot during dives.
Before level 4, your tools are Attack Wave, whose three eruptions slow by 20%, 40% and then 60%, and Sacred Hammer, whose recast knocks enemies airborne for 1 second. That is enough control for your marksman to win early trades. Use bushes along the gold lane to hide your approach, and charge so that the push carries the enemy toward your teammates rather than away from them. Once you have Implosion, move toward the side where your jungler is, since your full combo needs damage behind it.
::map roam | Roam with your marksman and set up kills.
## Mid game and teamfights
Wait for the enemy to group, especially around turtle and lord. Approach from a bush or the side, then charge, Implode and knock up. Your team must be ready to follow.
Sacred Hammer's charge pushes enemies along to the end of its path, so the charge itself bunches the enemy up before Implosion pulls them in. Implosion stuns for 2 seconds; during the first half of the channel, any control can interrupt it, so watch for enemy stuns before you start. If an enemy suppression hero is waiting, let them use their skill first or start the fight on the other side. After the combo, stay in front of your team: you have done your job, and your body now blocks skills aimed at your carries.
## Advanced techniques
- Flicker during Implosion: it changes where the pull happens.
- Second half: after the first half, only suppression can stop the channel.
- Fearless dives: four stacks block a turret shot.
- Bush engages: approach from unseen angles.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Lesley | bad=Zilong,Alucard,Lolita,Lesley,Franco | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Note: Lesley appears in both lists; the good list is an assessment, while the official data says she wins in ranked.
Playing against Tigreal: spread out, keep vision on bushes, and interrupt the first half of Implosion with control. Heroes who can leave a stun quickly, or who punish him with high mobility, make his engage much less reliable.
## Situational adjustments
- Against suppression: wait for the suppression to be used.
- Against magic damage: Radiant Armor earlier.
- When ahead: control objectives.
## Practice drills
- Charge drill: practice charge, Implosion and recast.
- Flicker drill: practice Flicker during Implosion.
## Common mistakes
- Engaging without the team.
- Walking in the open.
- Using Implosion on one hero.

guides.title: Lylia
guides.sub: Shadow-energy mage who chains detonations, then rewinds time to escape
guides.body:
## Identity: what Lylia is and why she is picked
Lylia is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane who deals damage by detonating Shadow Energy with her companion Gloom. Her passive, **Angry Gloom**, gives 15% movement speed inside Gloom's area, plus 5% each time Gloom is upgraded (up to 20%), for up to 35%.
**Magic Shockwave** sends Gloom in a line for 250-500 magic damage, slowing by 40% for 1.5 seconds and detonating any Shadow Energy it touches. **Shadow Energy** places energy that slows by 80% for 0.5 seconds; when detonated by Gloom or Magic Shockwave, it deals extra damage and turns into Gloom for 8 seconds, which can detonate more Shadow Energy in range, and each chained detonation within 8 seconds deals 30% more damage, up to 120%. Her ultimate, **Black Shoes**, returns her to where she was 4 seconds ago, restoring all 5 Shadow Energy charges and her HP and mana to that state, plus extra max HP, and she is untargetable while teleporting.
Why she is picked: very high area damage and an escape that undoes damage. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 11 times (5 wins) and banned 11 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, 11 picks (5 wins) and 13 bans. Her weakness: her combo takes practice, and she has no hard control.
## Kit deep-dive
### Angry Gloom (passive)
Movement speed in Gloom's area helps you kite.
### Magic Shockwave (Skill 1)
The detonator. Aim it through your Shadow Energy.
### Shadow Energy (Skill 2)
Place energy, then detonate. Chain detonations for more damage.
### Black Shoes (Ultimate)
A rewind: HP, mana and charges return to their state 4 seconds ago.
::curve 4,5,4 | Strong early wave clear and poke, very strong mid game, and still dangerous late.
## Combos
::combo Chain detonation | S2 > S2 > S1 > S2 > S2 | Place energy, detonate with the shockwave, then keep placing energy near Gloom.
::combo Rewind reset | S2 > S2 > S2 > ULT > S2 | Spend energy, rewind to restore all charges, spend again.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Lightning Truncheon, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Blood Wings | Burst and penetration.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Clear waves with Shadow Energy and Magic Shockwave, and poke the enemy mage.
Shadow Energy stores a charge every 9 seconds, up to 5, and costs only a 1-second cooldown between casts, so she can place several at once. Place two or three on the wave, then send Magic Shockwave through them: each detonation deals extra damage and turns into Gloom, which can detonate more energy nearby. Against the enemy mage, keep one or two charges for poke and the 80% slow, so they cannot step up to trade without being punished.
::map rotate | Clear mid, then rotate.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stand at the edge of fights and chain detonations on grouped enemies. Use Black Shoes after taking damage to rewind to safety.
The key to her teamfight is the chain: each time Gloom detonates another Shadow Energy within 8 seconds, the detonation damage rises by 30%, up to 120%. Place energy along the line the enemy will walk through, detonate the first one, and let Gloom jump from one to the next. Gloom's area also gives you 15% movement speed or more, which helps you stay at the right distance. Black Shoes returns you to where you stood 4 seconds ago with the HP and mana you had then and all 5 charges restored, so a common pattern is to spend every charge, take the enemy's burst, then rewind and spend them all again.
## Advanced techniques
- Rewind timing: use the ultimate after taking burst to restore HP. If you were already low 4 seconds ago, the rewind will not help, so think ahead.
- Chain stacking: each chained detonation in 8 seconds adds 30%, up to 120% on the fifth.
- Charge reset: the rewind restores all 5 charges, which makes it an offensive tool as well as an escape.
- Untargetable teleport: you cannot be targeted while teleporting, so the rewind dodges targeted ultimates.
- Speed after rewind: you gain extra movement speed for a few seconds after the rewind, useful to get away or re-enter.
## Draft and team fit
In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was drafted most often with Nolan (7 games together, 3 wins) and Atlas (4 games, 4 wins); in the MPL ID S18 playoffs with Freya and Paquito (5 games each).
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Aulus | bad=Barats,Chip,Hanabi,Alpha,Alice | ally=Atlas,Nolan,Freya,Paquito
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Lylia: bait her rewind, then kill her. Stand apart so her detonations do not chain through your team, and dive her when Black Shoes is on cooldown.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: hold the rewind and keep two Shadow Energy charges for the 80% slow.
- Against magic defense: Divine Glaive earlier.
- When ahead: push waves quickly and rotate to objectives, where enemies have to group.
## Practice drills
- Chain drill: practice chaining five detonations on grouped dummies.
- Rewind drill: practice spending all charges, then rewinding to spend them again.
## Common mistakes
- Using the rewind too early, before you have taken damage.
- Missing the detonation, so the energy only slows.
- Standing in front of your tank.

guides.title: Rafaela
guides.sub: Light support who heals, speeds up her team and revives a fallen ally
guides.body:
## Identity: what Rafaela is and why she is picked
Rafaela is a ranged magic support for the roam. Her passive, **Divine Resurrection**, lets her periodically use a special skill to instantly resurrect a fallen ally after a brief channel; they respawn at base with extra movement speed. Its cooldown depends on its base cooldown and the ally's remaining respawn time, and is not affected by cooldown reduction.
**Light of Retribution** strikes the three nearest enemies for 225-500 magic damage, reveals them briefly and slows them by 40% for 1.5 seconds; enemies hit again within 5 seconds take 20% more damage, stacking 3 times. **Holy Healing** restores 100-125 HP to nearby allies, plus 150-250 to herself and the most injured ally in range, and gives nearby allies 30% movement speed and slow immunity for 1 second. Her ultimate, **Holy Baptism**, fires a line for 460-660 magic damage and stuns for 1.5 seconds.
Why she is picked: healing, speed and a long line stun. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she has a 54.08% win rate and a 13.72% ban rate. Her weakness: fragile and without an escape.
## Kit deep-dive
### Divine Resurrection (passive)
Revive the ally who matters most.
### Light of Retribution (Skill 1)
Auto-targets the three nearest enemies.
### Holy Healing (Skill 2)
Heal and speed boost with slow immunity.
### Holy Baptism (Ultimate)
A long line stun.
::curve 3,4,4 | Solid throughout.
## Combos
::combo Stun and chase | ULT > S1 > S2 | Stun, strike, speed up your team.
## Builds and emblems
::build Healer | Magic Shoes, Enchanted Talisman, Fleeting Time, Flask of the Oasis, Oracle, Immortality | Healing and cooldowns.
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Agility, Pull Yourself Together, Focusing Mark | Speed and cooldowns.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Roam with your jungler and marksman.
Light of Retribution has a 4-second cooldown and hits the three nearest enemies automatically, so it is easy poke that also reveals enemies and slows them by 40%. Hitting the same enemy again within 5 seconds adds 20% more damage, up to 3 times, so use it often during trades. Holy Healing restores HP to nearby allies, heals the most injured ally and you more, and gives your team 30% movement speed and slow immunity for 1 second: use it to win a chase or to escape a gank.
::map roam | Roam with your team.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stay behind, heal, and stun with the ultimate.
Holy Baptism fires a long line that stuns every enemy hit for 1.5 seconds. Aim it through the enemy frontline into their backline, or use it to stop a diver who reached your carry. Because Light of Retribution targets automatically, you can stay at a safe distance and keep it on cooldown throughout the fight. Holy Healing's speed boost is also an engage tool: cast it as your team walks in so everyone arrives together and ignores slows for a moment.
Divine Resurrection changes how you should think about deaths. When your carry falls, check whether the revive is ready: they respawn at base with extra movement speed, which can bring them back to a long objective fight in time.
## Advanced techniques
- Revive timing: the revive's cooldown depends on the ally's remaining respawn time, so late-game deaths, with long respawn timers, are where it saves the most.
- Stacking Light of Retribution: three hits within 5 seconds stack the extra damage.
- Speed scaling: every 20 magic power adds 1% to Holy Healing's movement speed bonus, up to 80%.
- Long-range stun: the line is long, so use it from behind your frontline.
## Draft and team fit
Rafaela suits teams with an immobile carry who benefits from her speed boost and slow immunity, and teams that want to chase: Holy Healing makes the whole team faster for a moment. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, she has a 54.08% win rate with a 1.02% pick rate, one of the highest win rates of any support. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 4 times (2 wins) and banned 9 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, picked twice without a win.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Lesley | bad=Valir,Marcel,Natalia,Cici,Alpha | ally=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Lesley
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Rafaela: dive her. She has no escape, so heroes who reach the backline quickly kill her before she can heal or stun.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: stay near your tank and hold the ultimate for defense.
- Against poke: use Holy Healing often to keep your team healthy.
- When ahead: speed your team into objectives with Holy Healing.
## Practice drills
- Stun drill: practice the line stun through a group.
- Revive drill: in practice games, track the revive and use it on the carry.
## Common mistakes
- Wasting the ultimate on a single tank.
- Standing in front of the frontline.
- Forgetting the revive.

guides.title: Dyrroth
guides.sub: Abyss fighter who shreds physical defense and ends fights with a lost-HP strike
guides.body:
## Identity: what Dyrroth is and why he is picked
Dyrroth is a melee physical fighter for the EXP lane or jungle, built around short, violent trades. His passive, **Wrath of the Abyss**, enhances Burst Strike and Spectre Step once his Rage reaches 50%. Every 2 basic attacks he releases Circle Strike, which damages enemies around him and heals him for 50 plus 40% of the damage dealt. Each time he hits an enemy hero, Burst Strike and Spectre Step lose 1 second of cooldown, so the more he fights heroes, the more often he casts.
**Burst Strike** fires a burst for 200-450 physical damage and slows by 25% for 1.5 seconds; enhanced, it has longer range, deals 140% damage and doubles the slow. **Spectre Step** dashes and stops at the first non-minion target for 230-355 physical damage; recast to lock on with Fatal Strike for 345-570 physical damage, which reduces the target's physical defense by 40% for 4 seconds. Enhanced, Fatal Strike deals 150% damage, adds a 90% slow for 1 second and reduces physical defense by 60% instead. His ultimate, **Abysm Strike**, launches an uninterruptible strike after a short delay for 650-1250 physical damage plus 20% of the enemy's lost HP, slowing by 55% for 0.8 seconds.
Why he is picked: very high burst for a fighter, a defense shred that helps his whole team, and an ultimate that finishes wounded targets. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, he is picked in 1.07% of games with a 51.38% win rate. His weakness: once his dash is spent, he has no escape, and kiting heroes outlast his burst.
## Kit deep-dive
### Wrath of the Abyss (passive)
Rage at 50% enhances his two basic skills. Circle Strike every 2 attacks is his sustain, so keep attacking between skills.
### Burst Strike (Skill 1)
Poke and slow with a 5-second cooldown. The damage decays against the same target and is lower on minions, so it is better for trades than for waves.
### Spectre Step (Skill 2)
Dash, then Fatal Strike. The physical defense reduction lasts 4 seconds, which is the window for your ultimate and your team's damage.
### Abysm Strike (Ultimate)
Cannot be interrupted once cast. Its bonus damage is based on lost HP, so it is strongest as a finisher.
::curve 5,4,3 | Very strong early trades, strong mid-game pickoffs, and weaker late against tanky, grouped teams.
## Combos
::combo Full burst | S2 > S2 > S1 > BA > BA > ULT | Dash and Fatal Strike to shred defense, Burst Strike, two attacks for Circle Strike, then the ultimate.
::combo Enhanced opener | BA > BA > S2 > S2 > ULT | Build Rage first so Fatal Strike is enhanced for the 60% shred and 90% slow.
::combo Poke and finish | S1 > ULT | Slow with Burst Strike, then finish with the lost-HP strike.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst fighter | Warrior Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Queen's Wings, Immortality | Burst and penetration, with Queen's Wings and Immortality to survive after diving.
::build Sustain fighter | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Hunter Strike, Brute Force Breastplate, Queen's Wings, Immortality | More HP and spell vamp for long side-lane duels.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing on skill damage.
::spells Petrify, Retribution | Petrify in the EXP lane; Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Dyrroth is one of the strongest early fighters. Build Rage by attacking the wave, then trade when your skills are enhanced: an enhanced Fatal Strike cuts the enemy's physical defense by 60% and slows them by 90% for 1 second, which wins most short trades. Each hero hit takes 1 second off both basic skills, so a good trade gives you another cast before the enemy recovers. Back off once your dash is on cooldown.
::map lane | Pressure the EXP lane with enhanced trades.
## Mid game and teamfights
Look for picks on isolated squishy heroes, and in fights, wait for the enemy's crowd control to be used before you dash in. Use Fatal Strike on the target your team is focusing: the defense shred helps every physical damage dealer on your team for 4 seconds. Save the ultimate for a target below half HP, since it adds 20% of their lost HP as damage.
## Advanced techniques
- Rage management: enter fights with Rage above 50% so both skills are enhanced.
- Cooldown cuts: hitting heroes takes 1 second off both skills each time, so in a fight, your skills come back very quickly.
- Uninterruptible ultimate: once cast, it cannot be stopped, so you can fire it into enemy control.
- Circle Strike sustain: every 2 basic attacks heal you, which is why weaving attacks between skills matters.
## Draft and team fit
Dyrroth is a solo-queue fighter more than a pro pick: in the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked once and banned 5 times, and in the MPL ID S18 playoffs picked once and banned twice. He pairs well with physical damage junglers and marksmen who benefit from the defense shred, and with roamers who can lock a target for his combo.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Lukas | bad=Uranus,Alice,Esmeralda,Aldous,Phoveus | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Kaja,Chou
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: fighters who trade in melee range take his full burst. Note that Dyrroth is also in the official counter list for Masha.
Playing against Dyrroth: stay out of his early trades, kite him after his dash, and build physical defense; tanks with sustain, such as Uranus and Alice, outlast his burst.
## Situational adjustments
- Against sustain tanks: Malefic Roar earlier and do not overcommit.
- Against kiting teams: Petrify to lock targets.
- When ahead: invade the enemy jungle and pick off squishy heroes.
- When behind: farm side lanes and wait for your team's engage.
## Practice drills
- Rage drill: build Rage on a dummy and practice the enhanced Fatal Strike.
- Weave drill: weave two attacks between skills for Circle Strike.
## Common mistakes
- Diving with no Rage.
- Using the ultimate on full-HP targets.
- Chasing kiting heroes after the dash is used.

guides.title: Harley
guides.sub: Card-throwing mage assassin who burns a target with a ring of fire
guides.body:
## Identity: what Harley is and why he is picked
Harley is a ranged magic assassin and mage for the jungle or mid lane. His passive, **Magic Master**, makes his basic attacks deal 60 magic damage and lower the enemy's magic defense by 2 for 3 seconds, stacking 10 times.
**Poker Trick** throws 3-5 waves of cards, each dealing 130-210 magic damage to the first enemy hit and giving him 10% attack speed for 3 seconds. **Space Escape** blinks in a direction, leaving a magic hat and granting 30% movement speed for 2 seconds; recast within 4 seconds to return to the hat. His ultimate, **Deadly Magic**, fires a ring of fire at a target hero for 200-400 magic damage and a 40% slow for 1.5 seconds; it stays for 4 seconds, then explodes for 100-200 plus 50% of the damage the enemy took during that time.
Why he is picked: a reliable burst combo and an escape that returns him to safety. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, he is picked in 0.62% of games with a 48.21% win rate. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked 3 times and banned 5 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, picked twice (2 wins) and banned 5 times. His weakness: his ultimate can be blocked by other heroes, and he is fragile once his blink is used.
## Kit deep-dive
### Magic Master (passive)
Magic basic attacks and a magic defense shred.
### Poker Trick (Skill 1)
Waves of cards with an attack-speed bonus.
### Space Escape (Skill 2)
Blink in and return.
### Deadly Magic (Ultimate)
A ring that explodes for half of the damage dealt during it.
::curve 4,5,3 | Strong early, very strong mid and weaker late.
## Combos
::combo Ring burst | ULT > S1 > BA > S2 | Ring, cards, attack, then blink away.
::combo Blink in and out | S2 > ULT > S1 > S2 | Blink in, ring, cards, return to the hat.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Concentrated Energy, Blood Wings | Burst and penetration.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Retribution, Flicker | Retribution in the jungle; Flicker in mid.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Farm quickly and gank once you have the ultimate.
Poker Trick throws several waves of cards, and each hit gives Harley 10% attack speed for 3 seconds, so clearing camps with skills and attacks together is efficient. His basic attacks deal 60 magic damage and shred magic defense, stacking 10 times, which helps against the jungle creeps and against enemy heroes. Gank lanes where the enemy is low or pushed up: Space Escape lets you blink in and come back to the hat if the gank goes wrong.
::map jungle | Clear and gank.
## Mid game and teamfights
Flank and burst a squishy target, then return to the hat.
Deadly Magic is the center of his damage. It deals damage and slows the target by 40% for 1.5 seconds, then explodes after 4 seconds for extra damage plus 50% of all the damage the target took during that time, from Harley and from his teammates. Cast it when your team is about to focus the same target, then throw every Poker Trick wave and basic attack you can. Because the ring is a projectile, enemy heroes standing in front of your target can block it; look for an open angle from the side. Space Escape leaves a hat where you stood, so blink in for the ring, deal your damage, and return to the hat before the enemy answers.
## Advanced techniques
- Ring explosion: deal as much damage as possible during the 4 seconds, and call for your team to focus the same target.
- Hat return: blink in, burst, then return; the recast must happen within 4 seconds.
- Card falloff: enemies hit more than 3 times by Poker Trick take less damage from later hits, so spread cards when several enemies are close.
- Magic defense shred: each basic attack lowers magic defense by 2 for 3 seconds, up to 10 stacks, so weave attacks between skills.
- Movement speed: the blink also gives 30% movement speed for 2 seconds; if you do not need to return, keep the speed to escape.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Lesley,Hanabi | bad=Melissa,Valir,Alice,Suyou,Angela | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Kaja,Chou
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Harley: stand behind your teammates to block the ring. After his ultimate lands, use your escape or a shield early, since the explosion grows with the damage you take. Heroes who can catch him after he blinks, or tank his burst, are the cleanest answers.
## Situational adjustments
- Against magic defense: Divine Glaive earlier.
- Against assassins: Blood Wings earlier and keep Space Escape for defense.
- When ahead: invade the enemy jungle and pick off isolated heroes.
- When behind: farm safely and wait for your team's engage before using the ring.
## Practice drills
- Ring drill: practice dealing damage during the ring.
- Hat drill: practice blinking in and returning within 4 seconds.
## Common mistakes
- Ulting into heroes who block the ring.
- Forgetting to return to the hat.
- Diving without vision.

guides.title: Chou
guides.sub: Kung-fu fighter who kicks one enemy across the map into his team
guides.body:
## Identity: what Chou is and why he is picked
Chou is a melee physical fighter for the EXP lane or roam, known for one move: the kick that sends a carry into his team. His passive, **Only Fast**, makes his next basic attack deal 180% damage after he travels 5 units, briefly slowing by 80% and reducing physical defense, stacking twice.
**Jeet Kune Do** strikes up to 3 times for 180 physical damage each; the third cast knocks enemies airborne, and hitting a hero with it resets Shunpo. **Shunpo** charges with control immunity and a 200 physical damage shield. His ultimate, **The Way of Dragon**, kicks a target hero for 400 physical damage and knocks them back; recast to chase for a total of 480.
Why he is picked: the kick repositions an enemy carry, and his skills give him control immunity and a knock-up. In the MPL ID S18 playoffs he was picked 8 times (5 wins) and banned 10 times; in the MPL PH S18 playoffs, picked 5 times (2 wins) and banned 6 times. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, his win rate is 44.68%, a sign that his kick is hard to use well in solo queue. His weakness: a missed kick leaves him exposed, and his damage falls off late.
## Kit deep-dive
### Only Fast (passive)
Move 5 units for an empowered attack. It deals 180% damage, briefly slows by 80% and reduces physical defense, stacking twice. Walking around a target before attacking keeps it ready.
### Jeet Kune Do (Skill 1)
Three strikes; the third knocks airborne. Landing the third on a hero resets Shunpo, so it is both control and mobility.
### Shunpo (Skill 2)
A charge with control immunity and a 200 physical damage shield. Use it to walk through enemy control, or to escape after the kick.
### The Way of Dragon (Ultimate)
The kick deals 400 physical damage and knocks the target back; the recast follows them for a total of 480. The direction of the knock-back is the direction you face, so position before you kick.
::curve 4,4,3 | Strong early and mid, less decisive late.
## Combos
::combo Kick into team | Flicker > ULT | Flicker behind the target, kick them into your team.
::combo Knock-up | S1 > S1 > S1 > S2 | Three strikes, then reset Shunpo.
## Builds and emblems
::build Roam fighter | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Durability and damage.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense and sustain.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for the kick.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Trade with Jeet Kune Do. Walk around before attacking so Only Fast is ready, and finish a combo with the third strike to knock the enemy airborne and reset Shunpo. Chou's trades are short: hit, knock up, step away. As a roamer, look for picks with your jungler once you have the kick.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane or roam with your jungler.
## Mid game and teamfights
Kick the enemy carry into your team. The usual setup is to walk around the enemy frontline, often from a bush or by Flickering behind the target, so the kick sends them toward your teammates or under your turret. Shunpo's control immunity lets you get there through enemy stuns. If the carry is out of reach, kick the enemy hero who threatens your own backline away from it instead. After the kick, stay near the target with the recast so your team's damage finishes them.
## Advanced techniques
- Flicker kick: Flicker behind the target, then kick toward your team.
- Shunpo reset: hitting a hero with the third Jeet Kune Do resets Shunpo, giving you a second charge.
- Immunity window: Shunpo grants control immunity while charging, so use it when the enemy throws their control.
- Defensive kick: kicking a diver away from your carry can save a fight.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Lesley,Hanabi | bad=X.Borg,Fanny,Beatrix,Natalia,Benedetta | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Chou: stay near your team and avoid standing at the edge where a kick sends you into his team. Watch for him in bushes and keep control for after his Shunpo, when he no longer has immunity.
## Situational adjustments
- Against heavy control: save Shunpo for immunity.
- Against tanky teams: build more defense and focus on the kick as utility.
- When ahead: roam with your jungler for picks.
- When behind: farm safely and wait for your team's engage.
## Practice drills
- Kick drill: practice Flicker kicks in a training match.
- Reset drill: practice the three-strike combo into a Shunpo reset.
## Common mistakes
- Missing the kick, or kicking the target away from your team.
- Using Shunpo before the enemy uses their control.
- Fighting without Only Fast ready.

guides.title: Valentina
guides.sub: Shadow mage who steals the enemy's ultimate and turns it against them
guides.body:
## Identity: what Valentina is and why she is picked
Valentina is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane with one of the most unusual ultimates in the game: she copies an enemy hero's ultimate and casts it herself. Her passive, **Primal Force**, gives her 8-50 extra EXP each time she damages an enemy hero (every 2 seconds), and if the enemy's level is not higher than hers, 30% of the damage she deals is converted into HP. That means she out-levels her lane opponent and sustains through trades.
**Shadow Strike** fires a line for 340-665 magic damage and slows by 40% for 1 second; heroes hit are marked with a Shadow Sigil for 4 seconds and are terrified for 1 second if hit by Shadow Strike again during that time (once per 4 seconds). **Arcane Shade** dashes and fires 3 Shadow Bolts at nearby enemies for 125-225 magic damage each; it can be cast again within 6 seconds, and every bolt that hits reduces Shadow Strike's cooldown by 1 second. Her ultimate, **I Am You**, slows a target hero by 70% for 0.5 seconds and lets her cast their ultimate, taking their form and basic attack type for up to 12 seconds. The stolen ultimate is at her level, and its cooldown is 120%-100% of the original, never below 10 seconds.
Why she is picked: in the right draft, she gets a second copy of the enemy's best ultimate. Pro teams in the Philippines banned her 10 times and picked her 6 times (2 wins) in the MPL PH S18 playoffs; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs she was banned 9 times. Her weakness: her value depends on what the enemy drafts, and her ranked Mythical Glory+ win rate over the past 7 days is 45.42%, which shows she is hard to play well.
## Kit deep-dive
### Primal Force (passive)
Extra EXP every time you damage a hero, plus healing while you are not lower level. Poke early to get ahead in levels.
### Shadow Strike (Skill 1)
Two hits within 4 seconds terrify the target for 1 second. Bolts from Arcane Shade shorten its cooldown, which is how you get the second hit quickly.
### Arcane Shade (Skill 2)
A dash with three bolts and a recast. Use it to reposition, to chase, or to refresh Shadow Strike.
### I Am You (Ultimate)
Choose the ultimate before the fight. The best targets are ultimates that win fights on their own: area control, big burst or a global effect.
::curve 4,4,4 | Strong early thanks to extra EXP, flexible mid game, and as strong late as the ultimate she steals.
## Combos
::combo Terrify | S1 > S2 > S1 | Mark with Shadow Strike, dash so the bolts cut its cooldown, then hit again to terrify.
::combo Steal and cast | ULT > ULT > S1 > S2 | Copy the enemy's ultimate, cast it on their team (the second ULT), then follow with your own skills.
::combo Escape | S2 > S2 > S1 | Dash twice to get away, then slow the chaser.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Lightning Truncheon, Blood Wings | Burst and penetration for her skills and stolen ultimates.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Poke the enemy mid laner often. Each hit on a hero gives extra EXP, so you can reach key levels before your opponent, and while you are not behind in level, the passive heals you for 30% of the damage. Use Shadow Strike to clear the wave and hit the enemy at the same time when they line up.
::map rotate | Win the mid lane on levels, then rotate with your ultimate.
## Mid game and teamfights
Before every fight, decide whose ultimate you will steal. Area control ultimates, such as a tank's group pull, are often the best choice, since they can start or turn a fight. Steal at the start of the fight if you want to engage, or later if you want to counter-engage. After the steal, you keep your own skills, so combine the stolen ultimate with Shadow Strike's terrify.
## Advanced techniques
- Steal priority: choose the ultimate that changes the fight most, not the closest hero.
- Morph ultimates: if the stolen ultimate has a morph effect, her regular skills change too.
- Physical heroes: stealing from a physical damage hero also gives her physical attack.
- Cooldown awareness: the stolen ultimate has 100%-120% of the original cooldown, so a short-cooldown ultimate can be used often.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Atlas,Tigreal,Lolita,Johnson | bad=Carmilla,Lukas,X.Borg,Akai,Atlas | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Franco,Kaja
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Note: Atlas appears in both lists. His ultimate is one of the best to steal, but the official data says Atlas wins the matchup in ranked, so treat it as a skill matchup.
Playing against Valentina: stay out of her poke early, and dive her once her dash is on cooldown.
## Situational adjustments
- Against teams with weak ultimates: use her as a poke and burst mage instead.
- Against divers: keep Arcane Shade for escape.
- When ahead: rotate early and steal ultimates for objective fights.
## Practice drills
- Terrify drill: practice the double Shadow Strike.
- Steal drill: practice each enemy ultimate in custom games.
## Common mistakes
- Stealing an ultimate she cannot use well.
- Missing the second Shadow Strike.
- Dashing into the enemy team.

guides.title: Layla
guides.sub: Long-range marksman whose damage grows with distance
guides.body:
## Identity: what Layla is and why she is picked
Layla is a ranged physical marksman for the gold lane and one of the first heroes many players learn. Her passive, **Malefic Gun**, increases her damage the farther she is from her target, from 100% up to 130% at 6 units away (turrets excluded).
**Malefic Bomb** fires a bomb for 200-400 physical damage to the first enemy hit (it can crit); on a hit, her basic attacks and Void Projectile gain extra range for 3 seconds, and she gains 60% movement speed decaying over 1.2 seconds, doubled in duration if she hits a hero. **Void Projectile** explodes for 170-320 physical damage and applies a Magic Mark for 3 seconds; hitting a marked enemy deals 100-200 physical damage to nearby enemies and stuns them for 0.25 seconds. Her ultimate, **Destruction Rush**, fires a blast for 500-800 physical damage in a line; passively, it increases the range of her basic attacks and Void Projectile by 0.6-1.8 units and slightly increases her sight range.
Why she is picked: long range and simple mechanics. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she is picked in 1.15% of games with a 47.87% win rate. Her weakness: no dash, so she relies on positioning and her team.
## Kit deep-dive
### Malefic Gun (passive)
Stand far away: at 6 units, her damage is 130%.
### Malefic Bomb (Skill 1)
Poke, a speed boost and extra range for 3 seconds.
### Void Projectile (Skill 2)
Area damage with a mark and a short stun.
### Destruction Rush (Ultimate)
A long line blast, plus permanent extra range.
::curve 2,4,5 | Weak early, strong mid and very strong late at long range.
## Combos
::combo Poke | S1 > BA > S2 > BA | Bomb for range and speed, attack, projectile, attack.
::combo Finish | S2 > ULT | Mark and stun, then the line blast.
## Builds and emblems
::build Crit marksman | Swift Boots, Berserker's Fury, Windtalker, Haas' Claws, Malefic Roar, Wind of Nature | Crit and penetration.
::emblem Custom Marksman Emblem | Fatal, Weapon Master, Weakness Finder | Crit and attack.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Farm safely. Malefic Bomb is your poke and your escape: hitting a hero doubles the duration of the speed boost.
Layla's first minutes are about surviving to her items. Her range is longer than most marksmen once she lands Malefic Bomb, since a hit extends her basic attack and Void Projectile range for 3 seconds. Use that window to poke the enemy marksman from a distance they cannot answer, then step back. Void Projectile clears the wave with area damage; its mark stuns enemies near a marked target for 0.25 seconds when you hit it again, which can interrupt an enemy dash.
